question: When should you increase the following distance between you and the vehicle ahead?
options: a:When you are being tailgated by another driver.,b:When you are following a small passenger vehicle.,c:When you are driving more slowly than the posted speed limit.
note: If someone is following too closely, create extra space in front of you or change lanes to reduce the risk of a rear-end collision.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you miss your exit on the freeway you should not:
options: a:Back up on the road or shoulder.,b:Continue on and find an alternate route.,c:Proceed to the next exit and return to your destination.
note: Do not reverse on a freeway; proceed to the next exit and safely return to your route.

question: If you must make an emergency stop on an interstate you should:
options: a:Pull off the road, turn on your emergency flashers, and stay in your vehicle if you can.,b:Sound your horn at passing cars to get their attention.,c:Get out of your vehicle and flag down the first vehicle that passes.
note: If you stop on the shoulder, use flashers and remain inside your vehicle for safety unless danger requires otherwise.

question: When facing a green light with pedestrians in the intersection, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:You must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians.,b:You have the right-of-way over pedestrians.,c:Pedestrians must wait for you to cross.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians and vehicles already in the intersection, even when the light is green for drivers.

question: If a tire blows out, you should:
options: a:Hold the steering wheel tightly and use the brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brake and hold it.,c:Pull over quickly.
note: Grip the wheel, let the vehicle slow gradually, and use brakes lightly to maintain control before pulling over safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At what speed should you normally travel?
options: a:At a speed appropriate for road and weather conditions.,b:At the speed of vehicles surrounding you.,c:At the speed limit.
note: Drive at a safe speed for the current road, traffic, and weather conditions—never exceed the legal speed limit.

question: How often should you check your rearview mirrors?
options: a:Often to see how traffic is moving behind you.,b:Only when you are slowing down.,c:To see if a vehicle is in your blind spot.
note: Frequent mirror checks keep you aware of traffic patterns and potential hazards around your vehicle.

question: What are construction zone signs generally like in color and shape?
options: a:Diamond-shaped or rectangular with orange and black coloring.,b:Round or octagonal with black and yellow coloring.,c:Square or rectangular with white and red coloring.
note: Temporary work zone signs have orange backgrounds with black letters or symbols and are often diamond-shaped or rectangular.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for a green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: A red arrow pointing right at a traffic signal means you may:
options: a:Not turn in that direction until the light turns green.,b:Turn in that direction after slowing and checking for traffic.,c:Turn in that direction after you come to a complete stop.
note: A red arrow means stop for that direction; you must wait for a green signal or arrow to proceed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should a driver check blind spots when changing lanes?
options: a:Look only at the left outside mirror.,b:Look over the left or right shoulder toward the lane you want to enter.,c:Rely only on the inside rearview mirror.,d:Use the turn signal and assume it is clear.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; look over the appropriate shoulder to check for vehicles before changing lanes.

question: If oncoming headlights are blinding you at night you should:
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of the road.,b:Switch your lights to high beams.,c:Turn your lights on and off.
note: Look toward the right edge of the lane to avoid glare while keeping your car safely on the road.

question: Head restraints should be adjusted so they:
options: a:Contact the back of the head.,b:Are removed from the seats when possible.,c:Are anywhere since they have no effect.
note: Head restraints help prevent whiplash in rear-end collisions and should be positioned to touch the back of the head.

question: If you are angry after an argument, what should you do before driving?
options: a:Take a few minutes to cool off before driving.,b:Loudly play the radio while driving.,c:Drive on the interstate to let off steam.
note: Strong emotions reduce driving ability; calm down before operating a vehicle so you can focus on driving safely.

question: When is it legal to pass another vehicle?
options: a:You are on a road with a solid line next to your lane.,b:You are on a hill or curve.,c:You are on a road with a broken line next to your lane.
note: A broken line beside your lane indicates passing is allowed when it is safe; never pass on hills, curves, or where a solid line prohibits it.

question: When must you yield to a pedestrian?
options: a:At all times, even if the pedestrian is not obeying traffic laws.,b:Only if they are in a crosswalk.,c:Only if the traffic lights are in the pedestrian's favor.
note: Always do everything you can to avoid striking a pedestrian; yield even if they are not obeying traffic laws.

question: When you see a flashing yellow light at an intersection, how should you proceed?
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop, then enter the intersection when it is safe.,c:Yield to all traffic before crossing the intersection.
note: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution; you do not need to stop unless required by traffic conditions.

question: Alcohol is classified as which of the following?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:An antihistamine.,c:A depressant.,d:A vitamin.
note: Alcohol is a depressant that dulls judgment and slows reflexes, impairing driving skills.

question: Sudden strong wind gusts on highways can:
options: a:Cause problems for all vehicles.,b:Only affect the movement of large vehicles.,c:Only cause visibility problems.
note: Strong winds can affect vehicle stability and visibility for all types of vehicles, though large vehicles may be especially affected.

question: When parking on any hill you should:
options: a:Use your parking brake and leave the vehicle in park.,b:One of your rear wheels should touch the curb.,c:Make your front wheels parallel to the road if there is no curb.
note: Always leave the vehicle in gear or in park and set the parking brake when parked on a hill.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which statement about driving too slowly is true?
options: a:Driving too slowly on certain highways can be dangerous.,b:Driving too slowly is never unsafe.,c:The speed at which you drive does not affect safety.
note: Driving significantly slower than the flow of traffic can create hazards and lead to unsafe passing maneuvers by others.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you make room for vehicles entering the freeway from an on-ramp?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Merge into a different lane.,c:Slow down.
note: If it is safe, move into the next lane to create a gap for entering vehicles; if you cannot, adjust your speed to allow them to merge safely.

question: A road with double solid yellow centerlines means passing is:
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed from both directions.,c:Allowed only from your direction of travel.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate opposing traffic and prohibit passing from either direction.

question: When must you show proof of insurance to law enforcement?
options: a:If you are involved in a collision or stopped for a citation.,b:Only if you are involved in a collision.,c:Only if you are stopped and cited.
note: You must carry evidence of financial responsibility and show proof of insurance when requested by an officer after a stop or collision.

question: Roads are especially slippery just after it begins to rain. When the road is slippery you should:
options: a:Avoid making fast turns or stops.,b:Decrease the distance you look ahead of your vehicle.,c:Test your tires' traction while going uphill.
note: Wet roads reduce tire traction; drive slower and avoid rapid turns or stops until the surface improves.

question: When approaching a school crossing sign you should:
options: a:Always stop whether or not there is a stop sign.,b:Watch for children and be ready to stop.,c:Always sound your horn when children are present.,d:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: A pentagonal school crossing sign warns you to be alert for children and prepared to stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following is NOT a safe driving practice on the interstate?
options: a:Change lanes without signaling.,b:Slower traffic must keep to the right.,c:If you miss your exit, you must go to the next exit.
note: Always signal when changing lanes on the interstate; if you miss an exit, proceed to the next one—do not back up or turn around on the highway.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you not take?
options: a:Letting go of the steering wheel.,b:Applying your brakes.,c:Pressing your head firmly against the head restraint.
note: Do not let go of the steering wheel if struck from behind; brace against the seat and head restraint and be ready to steer.

question: What effect does slowing down to look at a crash or unusual event have on traffic?
options: a:Causes traffic congestion.,b:Improves traffic flow by preventing collisions.,c:Prevents rear-end collisions.
note: Avoid slowing to look at collisions or other unusual events (rubbernecking), because it creates congestion and hazards.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should a driver do when approaching a traffic signal that is not working?
options: a:Come to a full stop and yield the right-of-way before entering the intersection.,b:If the intersection is clear, the driver does not need to stop.,c:Drive quickly through the intersection to get out of the way of other vehicles.
note: Treat a non-functioning signal as a four-way stop: stop, yield as required, and proceed when safe.

question: In very foggy conditions you should slow down and use which lights?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Turn on your emergency flashers.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility, while hazard lights are not a substitute for headlights.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you use your turn signals when parking next to a curb?
options: a:Only when pulling away from the curb.,b:When pulling next to or away from the curb.,c:Only when pulling next to the curb.,d:Never required when parking.
note: Signal both when pulling up next to a curb and when pulling away so other road users know your intentions.

question: How must you treat an approaching flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red light has the same meaning as a stop sign: stop, yield to others, then proceed when safe.

question: At an intersection controlled by a flashing yellow light, what must you do?
options: a:Slow down and cross the intersection carefully.,b:Stop before crossing the intersection.,c:Wait for the green light before proceeding.
note: A flashing yellow light requires you to slow and proceed with caution, watching for cross traffic and pedestrians.

question: Before stopping at a traffic signal or sign, you should:
options: a:Check your mirrors for surrounding traffic.,b:Set the parking brake.,c:Press down hard on the accelerator.
note: Check mirrors first to be aware of traffic around you and then brake smoothly for a controlled stop.

question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot you should:
options: a:Move forward or drop back so the other driver can see you.,b:Keep a steady pace.,c:Stay in the driver's blind spot.
note: Do not linger in another vehicle's blind spot; change position so the driver can see you.

question: After having several beers, only what will reduce alcohol's effects?
options: a:Waiting several hours.,b:Drinking several cups of coffee.,c:Taking a cold shower.
note: Time is the only way to reduce BAC as the body metabolizes alcohol; coffee or a shower do not sober you up.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a fire hydrant?
options: a:15 feet,b:25 feet,c:30 feet
note: Parking within 15 feet of a fire hydrant is prohibited so hydrants are accessible for emergency use.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To safely enter a gap in highway traffic you should:
options: a:Watch only vehicles behind the intended gap.,b:Check behind you, then observe the vehicles ahead of the gap.,c:Speed up and force drivers to make room.,d:Assume gaps will appear automatically.
note: Before entering traffic, check behind and to the sides, then judge the space ahead to ensure you can safely merge.

question: Before changing lanes, you should check your mirrors and also:
options: a:Glance over your shoulder.,b:Always slow down in your traffic lane.,c:Never look over your right shoulder.
note: In addition to checking mirrors and signaling, glance over your shoulder to check blind spots before changing lanes.

question: On a multilane road, what does a dashed yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?
options: a:Passing is permitted only from the side next to the dashed line.,b:Passing is permitted from both directions.,c:Passing is prohibited from both directions.,d:The dashed side must yield to the solid side.
note: When solid and dashed yellow lines separate traffic, only the traffic next to the dashed line may pass; the side next to the solid line may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should not start across an intersection if you know you will block it when the light turns red:
options: a:Under any circumstances.,b:Unless you entered the intersection on a yellow light.,c:Unless you entered the intersection on a green light.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it without stopping; blocking intersections is prohibited.

question: What is the only thing that will lower your blood alcohol concentration (BAC)?
options: a:Time,b:Eating foods high in fat,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only time allows the body to metabolize and eliminate alcohol; food, coffee, or cold showers do not speed this up.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Why should you signal continuously while turning?
options: a:Because it is illegal to turn off your signal before finishing the turn.,b:So other road users know your intentions.,c:Because it is unsafe to turn off a signal early.,d:To avoid using your mirrors.
note: Continuous signaling when turning, changing lanes, slowing, or stopping informs other drivers, bicyclists, and pedestrians of your intentions.

question: If there is a deep puddle on the road ahead, you should:
options: a:Avoid the puddle if possible.,b:Maintain the posted speed to make it through the water.,c:Shift into neutral as you drive through the water.
note: Avoid driving through deep puddles when possible to prevent loss of control, engine damage, or hydroplaning.

question: As your driving speed increases, what becomes more important?
options: a:Look well ahead of your vehicle.,b:Turn on your headlights.,c:Change lanes frequently.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and hazards; looking farther ahead gives you more time to react.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Prior to entering a curve you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Activate your turn signal.,c:Brake hard.
note: Slow down before entering a curve so you can maintain control without hard braking while turning.

question: You must obey instructions from school crossing guards:
options: a:At all times.,b:Only during school hours.,c:Only when children are present.,d:Only if other traffic is minimal.
note: Drivers must always obey crossing guards' directions when present and controlling pedestrian crossings.

question: If you encounter an aggressive driver, what should you do?
options: a:Get out of their way.,b:Challenge them.,c:Speed up.
note: Avoid confrontation and safely yield or get out of the way to reduce the chance of escalation and collision.

question: What is a crosswalk?
options: a:The area where pedestrians may cross the roadway.,b:Another name for a four-way intersection.,c:An area designated for road construction workers.
note: A crosswalk marks where pedestrians may legally cross the street; crosswalks may be marked or unmarked at intersections.

question: As your blood alcohol concentration (BAC) rises, you become:
options: a:More intoxicated.,b:More coordinated.,c:More sober.
note: BAC measures the percentage of alcohol in the blood; higher BAC causes greater impairment.

question: At a railroad crossing with lowered gates and flashing lights, you should:
options: a:Come to a complete stop well behind the gates and wait until they are raised.,b:Slow down and drive around the gates.,c:Drive around the crossing gates if you can't see a train.
note: Do not go around lowered gates; remain stopped behind them until signals stop and gates are fully raised.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When should you yield your legal right-of-way?
options: a:Whenever it helps prevent collisions.,b:Often, even at controlled intersections.,c:Never; it confuses other drivers.
note: Yield your right-of-way whenever doing so will help avoid a crash; don't assume others will yield.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are being passed on both sides while driving in the center lane of an expressway, what should you do?
options: a:Move to the lane on your right.,b:Stay in the center lane.,c:Move to the lane on your left.
note: On multi-lane roads, remain in the right lanes unless passing or turning left; if traffic is passing you on both sides, move right when safe.

question: Which substances can impair your ability to drive?
options: a:Tranquilizers, marijuana, and sedatives.,b:Cough syrups and cold tablets containing codeine or antihistamines.,c:All of the above.
note: Many prescription, over-the-counter, and illegal drugs can impair driving ability, including sedatives, antihistamines, and some cold medicines.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane ahead, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing the street.,b:Make eye contact and then pass the pedestrian.,c:Slow down as you pass the pedestrian.
note: Even without a marked crosswalk, drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing their lane and allow them to cross safely.

question: If dust or smoke reduces visibility ahead, you should slow down and turn on which lights?
options: a:Headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Use headlights whenever visibility is poor so other drivers can see you; parking lights are insufficient and hazards lights are not a substitute for headlights.

question: If you begin to feel tired while driving, what is the safest choice?
options: a:Stop and either get rest or change drivers.,b:Drink something with caffeine.,c:Open a window.
note: To avoid fatigued driving, take breaks or switch drivers; short measures like caffeine or windows are not reliable substitutes for rest.

question: If the rear of your car begins skidding to the left while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Steer to the left.,b:Steer to the right.,c:Tap your brakes lightly and shift into neutral.
note: When your vehicle skids, steer in the direction you want to go (toward the skid) and avoid heavy braking unless necessary.

question: Your car may hydroplane at speeds as low as:
options: a:35 miles per hour.,b:40 miles per hour.,c:45 miles per hour.
note: Hydroplaning can begin at speeds around 35 mph when water prevents tires from contacting the road.

question: A steady red arrow displayed on a traffic light means:
options: a:Drivers cannot turn in the indicated direction.,b:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction after coming to a complete stop.,c:Drivers may turn in the indicated direction.
note: A steady red arrow prohibits movement in the arrow's direction until a green signal appears.

question: To turn quickly and safely, how should your hands be positioned on the steering wheel?
options: a:On opposite sides of the steering wheel.,b:On the top and bottom of the steering wheel.,c:Next to each other on the top of the steering wheel.
note: Place both hands on opposite sides of the wheel for better control and comfortable, safe turning, especially at higher speeds.

question: When driving on snowy or icy roads you should:
options: a:Use cruise control.,b:Make speed and directional changes more gradually than usual.,c:Drive as on dry roads.,d:Brake abruptly to stop quickly.
note: On snow or ice, make gradual speed and steering changes and never use cruise control; pump brakes if you don't have ABS.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How can you check your blind spot before changing lanes?
options: a:Turn your head and look over your shoulder.,b:Use your side mirror.,c:Use the inside rearview mirror.
note: Even with mirrors, some areas remain hidden; look over your shoulder to check blind spots before moving lanes.

question: When an emergency vehicle with flashing lights approaches, you must:
options: a:Maintain your speed and stay in lane.,b:Move into the right lane and slow down.,c:Pull over to the curb or edge of the road and stop until it passes.,d:Speed up to get out of the way.
note: When an emergency vehicle approaches with lights or siren, pull to the right edge of the road and stop until it has passed.

question: If you are feeling fatigued while driving, you should:
options: a:Find a safe parking area to take a short nap.,b:Increase the volume of your radio.,c:Increase your speed to reach your destination more quickly.
note: If you experience signs of fatigue, stop at a safe place to rest or switch drivers.

question: A solid yellow line next to a broken yellow line means which vehicles may pass?
options: a:Vehicles next to the broken line may pass.,b:Vehicles in both directions may pass.,c:Vehicles next to the solid line may pass.
note: Yellow center lines separate opposing traffic; a broken line beside your lane means you may pass when safe.

question: If you encounter a severe dust storm, what is the recommended action?
options: a:Slow down and pull completely off the road, turn off lights, take foot off the brake, and wait.,b:Maintain your speed and stay in your lane.,c:Turn on your high beams.
note: In a severe dust storm, drive off the road well out of traffic, turn off lights and brakes, stay buckled in the vehicle, and wait for conditions to improve.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Should you always drive more slowly than other traffic?
options: a:No, you can block traffic when you drive too slowly.,b:Yes, it is a good defensive driving technique.,c:Yes, it is always safer than driving faster than other traffic.
note: Driving excessively slowly may impede traffic flow and create hazards; drive at an appropriate speed for conditions.

question: If your vehicle's wheels run off the pavement, what is the first action to take?
options: a:Hold the steering wheel firmly, release the gas pedal, and gently apply the brakes.,b:Turn the front wheels slightly to the left to edge back onto the pavement.,c:Apply the brakes and turn the front wheels sharply to the left.
note: If you leave the roadway, keep the vehicle straight, ease off the gas, and brake gently until you can safely merge back into traffic.

question: A blood alcohol concentration of 0.02 percent:
options: a:Will double your chances of having an accident.,b:Won't have any effect on your driving.,c:Won't put other drivers at risk.
note: Even small increases in BAC raise the risk of being in a crash; 0.02% significantly increases risk.

question: When following a large truck on the freeway, how should your following distance compare to following a passenger car?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,b:Closer behind the truck than you would if following a passenger vehicle.,c:To the right side of the truck and wait to pass.
note: Trucks have larger blind spots and take longer to stop; maintain a greater following distance when behind them.

question: If you see heavy smoke covering the roadway ahead, you should:
options: a:Turn on four-way flashers and continue driving.,b:Reduce speed, move as far right as possible, and stop off the roadway.,c:Turn on high beams and continue.,d:Speed up to pass through quickly.
note: If the road ahead is obscured by smoke, slow down, move to the right, and stop off the roadway until it's safe to continue.

question: When a school bus has its red lights flashing, when may vehicles that are stopped behind it proceed?
options: a:When all students are off the bus.,b:When the stop arm is retracted.,c:When the stop arm is retracted and the bus starts moving.,d:When the bus driver waves you on.
note: You must remain stopped until the bus's red lights are off and the stop arm is retracted; do not proceed until it is safe.

question: How do you check your blind spots?
options: a:By looking in your side mirrors.,b:By turning your head and looking over your shoulder.,c:By looking only in your rearview mirror.,d:By using your high beams.
note: Blind spots are not visible in mirrors; turn your head and look over your shoulder to check them before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, you may safely return to your lane when you:
options: a:Can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:Have passed the other vehicle's front bumper.,c:Cannot see the vehicle directly to your right.
note: You should only return to your lane when you can see the passed vehicle's front or headlights in your mirror and it is safe.

question: Why should you increase following distance behind a large vehicle?
options: a:To better see around the sides of the vehicle.,b:Because other drivers will pull behind large vehicles.,c:To get caught in the vehicle's slipstream.,d:Because large vehicles always stop suddenly.
note: Large vehicles can block your view of the road ahead and their drivers may not see you; increase following distance to see around them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you drive much slower than the flow of traffic, you will most likely:
options: a:Interfere with traffic and receive a ticket.,b:Improve traffic flow.,c:Demonstrate defensive driving techniques.
note: Driving significantly slower than other traffic can block normal movement and may result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a main roadway from a private road, drivers should:
options: a:Assume they have the right-of-way.,b:Yield to traffic already on the road.,c:Honk to make other drivers move.,d:Enter at high speed to merge quickly.
note: Drivers entering from private roads must yield to traffic on the main roadway and to any pedestrians on sidewalks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Check your side mirror and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear.,b:Check the inside rearview mirror.,c:Slow down.
note: Always check mirrors and your blind spot by looking over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: Which is a dangerous habit when driving in work zones?
options: a:Both tailgating another vehicle and failing to watch for workers and moving equipment.,b:Tailgating another vehicle only.,c:Failing to carefully watch for workers and moving equipment only.
note: Tailgating and inattention to workers/equipment both increase the risk of crashes in work zones; avoid both behaviors.

question: If your vehicle begins to skid, what should you do?
options: a:Ease up on the gas pedal.,b:Turn off the ignition.,c:Brake as hard as possible.
note: If your vehicle starts to skid, release the accelerator or brake and allow speed to drop; avoid hard braking or turning off the ignition.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before returning to your original lane after passing, you should:
options: a:Beep your horn.,b:See both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:Flash your headlights.,d:Signal and immediately move over.
note: Only return when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror and it is safe.

question: If an oncoming vehicle has high beams on at night and you are affected, you should:
options: a:Look toward the left edge of your lane.,b:Look toward the right edge of your lane.,c:Look straight ahead into the headlights.,d:Flash your high beams in response.
note: Avoid looking directly at the bright lights; look toward the right edge of your lane and watch the vehicle from the corner of your eye.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you cross double yellow lines to pass another vehicle?
options: a:When the yellow line next to your side of the road is broken.,b:When the vehicle in front of you moves to the right to let you pass.,c:When the yellow line next to the opposite side of the road is broken.
note: You may pass across the centerline only if the broken (dashed) yellow line is on your side of the roadway and it is safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What are blind spots?
options: a:Areas of the road that cannot be seen in a vehicle's mirrors.,b:Spots in your vision when you become fatigued.,c:Traffic control devices.
note: Blind spots are areas near your vehicle not visible in mirrors; look over your shoulder before changing lanes.

question: If your vehicle's suspension is worn, what problem may occur?
options: a:Vehicle control problems.,b:Squealing brakes.,c:Slack in the steering only.,d:Engine overheating.
note: Bad suspension can cause poor vehicle control and excessive bouncing; you may need repair to restore safe handling.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection, you should:
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Oncoming traffic and pedestrians should yield to you.,c:Never yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.
note: Yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians before making a left turn; wait for a safe gap or signal permission.

question: On a roadway with a single broken white centerline you may:
options: a:Cross the centerline to change lanes.,b:You must stay within your lane.,c:Change lanes only from the left lane.
note: Broken white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and allow lane changes when safe.

question: Before driving, remove snow, frost, and ice from:
options: a:All windows.,b:Just the windshield.,c:Just the windshield and passenger window.
note: You must clear all windows and mirrors so you have unobstructed visibility before driving.

question: If your vehicle has a two-part safety belt system, how should you use it?
options: a:Use both the lap and shoulder belts.,b:Use only the lap belt.,c:Use only the shoulder belt.
note: Wear both the lap and shoulder portions of a two-part seat belt. Using only one part greatly reduces protection.

question: Which practice best describes where a driver should look while driving?
options: a:Watch beside, ahead, and to the rear of the car.,b:Only focus on the middle of the road.,c:Stare directly in front of the car.
note: Good drivers continuously scan ahead, to the sides, and behind to be aware of changing traffic conditions and potential hazards.

question: Why should you look farther ahead on a freeway than on a city street?
options: a:To see potential hazards earlier.,b:Because it takes a quarter mile to stop.,c:To help you keep up with traffic speed.,d:To avoid checking mirrors frequently.
note: On freeways you travel faster; watching farther ahead helps you detect hazards and adjust speed or position sooner.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Turning right on a red light is permitted:
options: a:Except where prohibited by a sign.,b:Only where indicated by a sign.,c:Only on a divided road.
note: Right turns on red are allowed after a full stop unless signs specifically prohibit the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle, how do you know you have enough space to return to the lane?
options: a:If you can see both of the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.,b:If you look over your shoulder and see the passed car behind you.,c:If the other driver signals for you to re-enter the lane.
note: Return to your lane only when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror, indicating safe clearance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should never change lanes while:
options: a:Within an intersection.,b:Checking your blind spot by looking over your shoulder.,c:Checking for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Changing lanes inside an intersection is prohibited and unsafe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers must obey instructions from:
options: a:Flaggers (signal persons) at construction sites.,b:Security guards patrolling parking lots.,c:Other drivers whose vehicles are broken down on the roadway.
note: Flaggers provide directions for safe movement through work zones and must be obeyed.

question: If you are about to be hit from the rear, which action should you avoid?
options: a:Release your seat belt.,b:Brace yourself.,c:Press your head against the head restraint.
note: Do not release your seat belt; brace and press your head against the head restraint to reduce risk of injury and whiplash.

question: A stopped school bus ahead on your side of the road is flashing red lights. What must you do?
options: a:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,b:Slow to a speed no faster than 10 mph.,c:Stop until the lights stop flashing.
note: When a school bus activates its red overhead lights and extends its stop arm to load or unload students, you must remain stopped until the lights stop flashing and the stop arm is retracted. Never pass a bus using these signals.

question: Which behavior may indicate an aggressive driver?
options: a:Their erratic and improper lane changes.,b:Their tendency to drive slowly.,c:The number of passengers in their car.
note: Aggressive drivers often make dangerous, erratic lane changes or otherwise drive in a threatening manner.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Unless a sign prohibits it, from where may you turn left on a red light?
options: a:From a one-way road to a one-way road.,b:From a two-way road to a one-way road.,c:Except in school zones.
note: You may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street after stopping and yielding, unless posted otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When must you stop before crossing railroad tracks?
options: a:When there isn't room on the other side to completely clear the tracks.,b:Only in cities with frequent train traffic.,c:If you are transporting two or more young children.,d:Never required if no train is visible.
note: Stop before railroad tracks if you cannot fully clear the tracks on the other side; never stop on the tracks.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you are approaching an intersection at the posted speed limit and the light turns yellow you should:
options: a:Stop before entering the intersection, if you can do so safely.,b:Speed up to cross before it turns red.,c:Slow down and proceed through without caution.
note: A solid yellow means caution; stop if it is safe to do so, otherwise proceed carefully through the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Driving much more slowly than surrounding traffic is:
options: a:Often a hazard because other drivers may become frustrated and try to pass you.,b:Appropriate if you don’t know the speed limit.,c:A good idea if the weather is bad.
note: Driving unusually slowly can create dangerous passing attempts by other drivers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you treat a flashing red traffic light?
options: a:Slow and yield the right-of-way.,b:Drive carefully through the intersection.,c:Come to a complete stop, check traffic, then go when safe.,d:Treat it as a green light.
note: A flashing red light means the same as a stop sign: stop, yield to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing another vehicle, when is it safe to return to your lane?
options: a:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you see the passed vehicle's headlights in your inside rearview mirror.,c:After you have signaled for three seconds.,d:When the driver you passed waves you back.
note: Before you return to your driving lane, be sure you are not too close to the vehicle you passed; when you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror, you likely have enough room to move back safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: After passing a vehicle in the same direction, when is it safe to move back into the right lane?
options: a:After about three seconds.,b:When you can see the entire front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,c:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,d:When the passed driver signals you to move back.
note: Do not return to your original lane until you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror and it is safe to do so.

question: To prevent hydroplaning on wet roads, what is the best action?
options: a:Slow down.,b:Move to the shoulder when it starts to rain.,c:Use cruise control to maintain a constant speed.
note: Hydroplaning is caused by driving too fast on wet pavement. Reduce speed in wet weather to help tires maintain road contact.

question: Which of the following will reduce a person's blood alcohol content (BAC)?
options: a:Eating foods high in fat,b:Time,c:Drinking caffeine
note: Only the passage of time removes alcohol and its impairing effects from the body; food, caffeine, or other measures do not speed up elimination.

question: You plan a right turn and a pedestrian with a guide dog is waiting to cross. What must you do?
options: a:Wait until the person crosses the street.,b:Turn off your engine until the person crosses the street.,c:Tell the pedestrian when to cross the street.
note: Pedestrians using guide dogs or white canes have the right-of-way; you must wait until they have crossed before making your turn.

question: When backing up you should:
options: a:Look through the rear window.,b:Rely only on your rearview mirror.,c:Press hard on the gas pedal.
note: Place your arm over the seat and look directly through the rear window while reversing at low speed.

question: Why is using a cell phone while driving distracting?
options: a:It makes the driver worry about call cost.,b:It occupies the driver's eyes, hands, and mind.,c:It draws the attention of other drivers.,d:It helps drivers stay alert.
note: Cell phone use while driving takes attention from driving tasks—your eyes, hands, and mind are distracted—increasing crash risk.

question: To improve visibility reduced by rain or fog, drivers should use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low beams reduce glare in rain or fog and help other drivers see your vehicle; high beams can worsen glare.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto an interstate, after checking for a gap, signaling, and adjusting speed, what should you do?
options: a:Merge carefully into the gap.,b:Wait for the lane to clear before merging.,c:Expect traffic to allow you to proceed since you have the right-of-way.
note: Identify a gap, accelerate to traffic speed, signal, and merge carefully; do not assume others will yield for you.

question: If you see pedestrians in a crosswalk ahead, a motorist should:
options: a:Continue; vehicles have right-of-way.,b:Wait until the pedestrians have crossed the street.,c:Pull to the right and go around the pedestrians.,d:Honk to get them to move faster.
note: Drivers must yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk and wait until the crosswalk is clear before proceeding.

question: On a solid green arrow you must:
options: a:Yield to any vehicle, bicycle, or pedestrian still in the intersection.,b:Wait four seconds before proceeding.,c:Yield to pedestrians only in the intersection.
note: A green arrow gives the right to go but you must yield to any traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers turning left must yield to:
options: a:Oncoming cars.,b:Overtaking cars.,c:No one.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming vehicles going straight through the intersection.

question: To whom should you give the right-of-way regarding pedestrians?
options: a:Any pedestrian crossing any street or in any crosswalk or intersection.,b:Only pedestrians in a marked crosswalk.,c:Pedestrians only if they have a crossing guard present.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in any marked or unmarked crosswalk and generally yield to pedestrians crossing the street.

question: When should you not use your horn?
options: a:When visibility ahead is limited.,b:If you might hit another vehicle.,c:Near blind pedestrians.,d:When another driver is merging.
note: Avoid using your horn near blind pedestrians; it can be dangerous. Yield to them and proceed when safe.

question: What are truck \no zones\"?"
options: a:Areas where cars disappear into blind spots or restrict a truck's ability to stop and maneuver safely.,b:Areas where there are several car lengths between their vehicle and the truck.,c:Areas with sufficient space to travel behind the truck.
note: \No zones\" are the large blind spots around trucks and buses where smaller vehicles are not visible to the driver and can be dangerously close."

question: Like alcohol and drugs, drowsiness can:
options: a:Impair your judgment.,b:Help you to be a better driver.,c:Make you feel better.
note: Not getting enough sleep slows reaction time, reduces awareness, and impairs judgment much like drugs or alcohol.

question: What do 'No passing zone' signs indicate?
options: a:To speed up slightly.,b:That it is not safe to pass.,c:To maintain a steady speed.,d:To only pass on the left.
note: A 'No passing zone' sign indicates an area where passing is illegal because visibility or road conditions make passing unsafe.

question: What is the only medically proven way to remove alcohol or drug combinations from your system?
options: a:Drink coffee.,b:Let your body have time.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Exercise vigorously.
note: The only way to lower blood alcohol concentration is to allow time for your body to metabolize the alcohol; nothing else speeds this process.

question: When must vehicles in Arizona be covered by liability insurance?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only when driven by a minor.,c:Only when driven on an interstate.
note: Every motor vehicle operated in Arizona should have an Arizona-based liability insurance policy at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left from a two-way street onto a one-way street, which lane should you enter?
options: a:Turn into the first (closest) lane.,b:Turn into any lane.,c:Turn into the second lane.
note: When turning onto a one-way street from a two-way street, turn into the first legal lane closest to you.

question: If the roadway is wet or icy, you should:
options: a:Reduce your speed.,b:Drive at the posted speed.,c:Speed up to get through faster.,d:Use cruise control for stability.
note: On wet, snowy, or icy roads, reduce speed because tires have less grip and stopping distances increase.

question: Where are a truck's blind spots typically located?
options: a:Both on the immediate left of the cab and directly behind the body.,b:On the immediate left of the cab.,c:Directly behind the body.
note: Large trucks have substantial blind spots on their left side and directly behind them; if you cannot see the driver's face in the side mirror, the driver likely cannot see you.

question: If a vehicle suddenly cuts in front of you, what should you do first?
options: a:Take your foot off the gas pedal.,b:Honk and step on the brake firmly.,c:Swerve into the lane next to you.
note: Removing your foot from the accelerator creates space and reduces the chance of a collision without abrupt braking.

question: If an oncoming driver fails to dim headlights, you should:
options: a:Look toward the right side of the road.,b:Look toward the center of the roadway.,c:Look straight ahead.
note: Glance toward the right edge of the road to avoid being blinded while still keeping your vehicle on course.

question: Which driving skills can be impaired by alcohol or drugs?
options: a:Both alertness and coordination.,b:Alertness.,c:Coordination.
note: Alcohol and drugs negatively affect many driving skills, including reaction time, coordination, alertness, and concentration.

question: When approaching a vehicle from behind at night, when should you switch from high to low beams?
options: a:Within 500 feet.,b:Within 100 feet.,c:Within 200 feet.,d:Within 50 feet.
note: Lower your high beams when you are within 200 feet of another vehicle ahead of you to avoid dazzling the driver.

question: When may you legally drive around or under a lowered railroad crossing gate?
options: a:Never.,b:When you can see clearly in both directions.,c:When the warning lights are not flashing.
note: It is illegal and extremely dangerous to go under or around lowered railroad crossing gates at any time.

question: When passing a motorcycle, you must:
options: a:Have your vehicle entirely in the left lane before and during the pass.,b:Blow your horn to make the motorcycle move onto the shoulder.,c:Give the motorcycle a full lane of space when passing.
note: Motorcyclists are entitled to a full lane; give them an entire lane when passing to avoid crowding them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A U-turn is not permitted:
options: a:On or near any curve or hill.,b:In a parking lot.,c:On a straight roadway with a clear view for 500 feet in both directions.
note: Never make a U-turn on or near a curve or hill where you cannot see approaching traffic.

question: You should not make sudden stops in front of large trucks and buses because:
options: a:Large trucks and buses require longer distances to stop than smaller passenger vehicles.,b:Small vehicle drivers cannot adequately see large trucks and buses in their rearview mirrors.,c:Large trucks and buses travel at a higher speeds than small vehicles.
note: Due to their weight and size, large vehicles need much more distance to stop than smaller cars.

question: On slippery surfaces such as snow or ice, you should:
options: a:Shift to a lower gear before descending steep hills.,b:Follow other vehicles more closely to maintain traction.,c:Pump your brakes only if you have anti-lock brakes.,d:Use cruise control for steady speed.
note: On slippery roads, shift to a low gear before steep descents; increase following distance and, if no ABS, pump brakes to avoid skids.

question: Interstate driving requires drivers to:
options: a:Be able to safely travel at higher speeds.,b:Be constantly alert.,c:Both be able to safely travel at higher speeds and remain constantly alert.,d:Have an HOV pass.
note: Safe interstate driving requires the ability to drive at higher speeds and constant alertness for rapid traffic changes.

question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean when the broken line is beside your lane?
options: a:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the lane next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means traffic next to the broken line may pass, while traffic next to the solid line may not.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What should you do before changing lanes or passing another vehicle?
options: a:All of the above.,b:Check your blind spots and mirrors.,c:Signal your intention before changing lanes.
note: Always signal, check mirrors, and check blind spots before any lateral move to alert other drivers and avoid collisions.

question: Consistently looking far ahead while on the highway primarily helps you to:
options: a:Reduce the need for last-minute braking or turning.,b:Spot upcoming police officers.,c:Help you keep up with traffic.
note: Scanning far ahead reduces sudden maneuvers by allowing earlier detection of changing traffic and hazards.

question: After snow or rain, which area is most likely to be slippery?
options: a:A road in a shaded area,b:A hilly, open road,c:A residential road
note: Shaded areas hold ice and remain frozen longer than sun-exposed roadways, increasing slipperiness.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a T intersection from the street that ends, what must a driver do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to cross traffic.,b:Have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into traffic.
note: Drivers on the street that ends must stop or yield and allow cross traffic to pass before proceeding.

question: If you experience a tire blowout, what is the correct action?
options: a:Slow down gradually and use your brakes lightly.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Tap or pump the brakes.
note: On a blowout, ease off the accelerator and slow gradually; avoid hard braking until the vehicle has slowed substantially.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a freeway, what should you do to check freeway traffic?
options: a:Use your side mirror and look over your shoulder.,b:Use your rearview mirror only.,c:Using your rearview and side mirrors is sufficient.
note: Use mirrors and a shoulder check to see blind spots and anticipate traffic when merging onto a freeway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A driver entering freeway traffic from an entrance ramp should:
options: a:Yield to drivers already on the interstate.,b:Have the right-of-way.,c:Force their way into traffic when necessary.
note: Drivers entering the freeway must yield to traffic already on the freeway and merge when safe.

question: When should drivers adjust mirrors, seats, and steering wheel?
options: a:Before starting the vehicle.,b:Before reaching speeds of 55 mph or above.,c:While backing out of a driveway.
note: Adjust the seat, mirrors, and steering wheel before you start driving to ensure proper control and visibility.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: On a one-way street, you may turn left onto another one-way street only if what is true about the other street?
options: a:Traffic on that street moves to the left.,b:Traffic on that street moves to the right.,c:You increase your speed before the turn.
note: You may turn left onto a one-way street only if traffic on that street flows leftward and there are no signs prohibiting the turn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When preparing to make a left turn from a two-way street, where should you position your vehicle?
options: a:Near the right-hand side of the road.,b:Near the centerline in the lane closest to the center.,c:On the left of the centerline.,d:In the turn lane two lanes over.
note: Begin a left turn from the lane nearest the centerline and turn into the first legal lane on the new roadway.

question: When parking downhill on a two-way road with no curb, turn your front wheels:
options: a:Toward the edge of the road (right).,b:Straight ahead.,c:Toward the center of the road (left).
note: When parked downhill without a curb, turn wheels toward the road edge so the vehicle rolls away from traffic if brakes fail.

question: What can happen if you take prescription drugs while drinking alcohol?
options: a:There will likely be no effect.,b:It may make you more alert.,c:It can make you unfit to drive.,d:It will cancel out alcohol's effects.
note: Combining alcohol with medications can increase impairment and make you unfit to drive safely.

question: Fatigue increases the risk of:
options: a:Falling asleep behind the wheel and crashing.,b:Being late for an appointment.,c:Missing an exit.
note: Fatigue slows decision-making and increases the chance of falling asleep while driving, which can cause serious crashes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How far before a turn should you activate your turn signal?
options: a:100 feet.,b:50 feet.,c:20 feet.
note: Signal at least 100 feet before turning to inform other road users of your intentions.

question: If you are already in an intersection when a green light changes to yellow, what should you do?
options: a:Continue moving and clear the intersection safely.,b:Stop.,c:Increase your speed so as not to cause an accident.
note: If you are in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through and clear the intersection as safely and quickly as possible.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which is true about changing lanes safely?
options: a:You only need to look over your right shoulder for any lane change.,b:Look over the shoulder in the direction you plan to move (right for right, left for left).,c:If you have two outside mirrors, you have no blind spots.,d:Rely on the turn signal alone.
note: Before changing lanes, signal, check all mirrors, and look over the shoulder toward the lane you plan to enter to check blind spots.

question: It is more dangerous to drive at night because:
options: a:You cannot see as far ahead at night.,b:The road is always more slippery at night.,c:Your reaction time is slower at night.
note: Reduced visibility after dark limits how far ahead you can see, increasing driving risk.

question: If poor weather reduces visibility, what should you do?
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Drive in the lane closest to oncoming traffic.,c:Speed up to get off the road quickly.
note: When visibility is reduced by weather or darkness, increase your following distance to allow more reaction time.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing yellow light, you must:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop at the intersection.,c:Maintain your normal speed.
note: A flashing yellow signal instructs drivers to slow down and be cautious; stopping is not required unless conditions warrant it.

question: How should you react to a sudden tire blowout while driving?
options: a:Use the brakes lightly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Apply the brakes firmly.
note: If a tire blows out, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the gas, and slow down gradually using light braking until you can stop safely.

question: What lights should you use as daylight starts to fade to help others see you?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Parking lights.,c:Emergency flashers.
note: Turn on low beams as daylight fades so other road users can see your vehicle; use high beams only when appropriate.

question: What does a yellow left-turn arrow mean?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Drivers should prepare to yield to oncoming traffic.,c:The protected left turn is about to end.
note: A yellow left-turn arrow signals the protected left-turn phase is ending; drivers must prepare to yield to oncoming traffic when it changes.

question: If you are under 21, your license can be suspended for driving with a blood alcohol level of:
options: a:0.15% or more.,b:0.08% or more.,c:Any detectable amount.,d:0.02% or more.
note: Arizona has zero tolerance for drivers under 21; any detectable amount of alcohol can lead to license suspension and penalties.

question: Because motorcycles, scooters, and mopeds are hard to see, you should:
options: a:Share a lane with them when possible.,b:Make continuous visual checks for them.,c:Slow down and let them pass only.,d:Honk to alert them of your presence.
note: Motorcycles can be hidden in blind spots or missed in a quick glance; drivers should constantly look for them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When merging onto the freeway you should be driving:
options: a:At or near the speed of traffic on the freeway.,b:Five to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.,c:The posted speed limit for freeway traffic.
note: Enter the freeway at or near the speed of existing traffic to merge smoothly and safely.

question: A driver license is considered which of the following?
options: a:Requirement.,b:Privilege.,c:Right.
note: Driving is a privilege that may be suspended or revoked if you do not obey laws or otherwise abuse driving privileges.

question: Which statement about large trucks is true?
options: a:They take longer to stop than passenger vehicles.,b:They all have air brakes that allow them to stop quickly.,c:They are more maneuverable than passenger vehicles.
note: Large trucks require longer stopping distances than passenger cars due to their size and weight.

question: Night driving is more difficult because:
options: a:Distance and vehicle speed are harder to judge in the dark.,b:The speed limit is increased at night.,c:There are fewer cars on the roads at night.
note: Reduced visibility at night makes judging distance and speed of other vehicles more difficult.

question: Which passengers are required to wear safety belts in Arizona?
options: a:Passengers in the front seat and passengers age 16 and below.,b:Only a passenger in the front seat.,c:Only passengers age 16 or below.
note: In Arizona, all front-seat occupants and any passenger age 16 or younger must wear a fastened safety belt.

question: When visibility is low due to fog, you should:
options: a:Use high beam headlights to see further.,b:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,c:Increase your speed so others can avoid you.,d:Turn off headlights and use parking lights.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beams; if visibility is extremely poor, pull off the roadway until conditions improve.

question: To reduce the chance of losing traction on wet roads you should:
options: a:Make abrupt turns.,b:Apply the brakes firmly and quickly.,c:Slow down.,d:Drive faster to reduce hydroplaning risk.
note: To avoid hydroplaning and traction loss, reduce your speed and keep tires in good condition; avoid abrupt steering or braking.

question: When double solid yellow lines separate lanes of traffic:
options: a:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,b:Passing is permitted from the left.,c:Passing is permitted from the right.
note: Double solid yellow lines indicate no passing by traffic in either direction.

question: Why should you never use high beam headlights in fog or mist?
options: a:The light will reflect back into your eyes.,b:Approaching vehicles might not see you.,c:Vehicles behind may follow too closely.,d:High beams melt fog.
note: High beams reflect off fog back into your eyes and reduce your visibility; use low beams instead.

question: When passing a row of parked vehicles, you should:
options: a:Be prepared for people or vehicles to enter your lane unexpectedly.,b:Expect all pedestrians to yield to you.,c:Drive close to parked vehicles to leave more room for moving traffic.,d:Assume parked car doors will remain closed.
note: Give space and be ready for a person or vehicle to suddenly emerge from between parked cars.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: An important step when turning is to:
options: a:Check traffic in all directions.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Always move to the left lane.
note: Before turning, look to the rear and both sides to ensure the maneuver can be made safely.

question: When preparing to turn left, to whom must you yield?
options: a:Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting for a "Walk" signal.,b:Oncoming vehicles also turning left.,c:All approaching vehicles.
note: When turning left you must yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing with the signal and to other road users who have the right-of-way.

question: Which of these road surfaces freezes first?
options: a:A bridge,b:An intersection,c:A tunnel
note: Bridges and overpasses often freeze before the rest of the roadway because they are exposed on all sides.

question: Tailgating other drivers (following too closely) can:
options: a:Frustrate other drivers and make them angry.,b:Never result in a citation.,c:Reduce collisions by preventing being cut off.,d:Improve fuel economy.
note: Tailgating increases risk and can provoke aggressive responses; it may also lead to traffic citations for unsafe driving.

question: When near a large commercial vehicle you should:
options: a:Avoid driving beside it for long stretches of time.,b:Follow the large vehicle closely to reduce wind drag on your vehicle.,c:Drive on its right side when on curves and hills.
note: Large vehicles have significant blind spots; avoid lingering alongside where drivers cannot see you.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing, return to the right lane when:
options: a:You can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:You are one vehicle length ahead of the passed vehicle.,c:You are 50 feet ahead of the passed vehicle.
note: Only move back into the driving lane when you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror.

question: When a large truck is turning right onto a multi-lane street, how might it complete the turn?
options: a:It may have to swing wide to complete the right turn.,b:It may complete its turn in either of the two lanes.,c:It must stay in the right lane at all times while turning.
note: Long vehicles often need to swing wide on right turns because their rear wheels follow a shorter path than the front wheels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At intersections, crosswalks, and railroad crossings you should always:
options: a:Look to the sides of your vehicle to see what is coming.,b:Stop, listen, and proceed cautiously.,c:Slowly pass vehicles that seem to be stopped for no reason.
note: Always scan left and right at places where people or vehicles may enter your path.

question: Which of these statements about drinking and driving is true?
options: a:Alcohol affects judgment, which is needed to drive safely.,b:If you can walk in a straight line after drinking, it is safe to drive.,c:If you are under the legal blood alcohol concentration limit, your driving isn't impaired.
note: Alcohol impairs judgment and decision-making needed for safe driving, even at low levels.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You may drive off the paved roadway to pass another vehicle:
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the vehicle ahead is turning left.,c:If there are two or more lanes traveling in your direction.
note: You must not leave the main-traveled portion of the road to pass; passing off the pavement is illegal and unsafe.

question: Which statement is true about roadwork zones?
options: a:You must Slow for the Cone Zone.,b:Fines are the same in work zones as normal traffic conditions.,c:Slow down only if you think workers are present.
note: Work zones often have increased fines and signage urging drivers to slow down; always reduce speed and drive cautiously through them.

question: Approaching an intersection with a flashing red signal, what must you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop, yield to oncoming traffic or pedestrians, then proceed.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed with caution.,c:Come to a complete stop and remain stopped as long as the light is red.
note: A flashing red signal is treated as a stop sign: stop, yield to others, and proceed when clear.

question: The best way to avoid a dangerous situation while driving is to:
options: a:Know what is happening around your vehicle.,b:Turn off the radio.,c:Keep your eyes focused only ahead.,d:Drive faster than other vehicles.
note: Constantly scanning front, sides, and rear helps you detect problems early and respond to avoid danger.

question: To see vehicles in your blind spots, you should:
options: a:Look over your shoulders.,b:Check the outside rearview mirror.,c:Check the inside rearview mirror.
note: Blind spots are areas not visible in mirrors; a shoulder check is needed before changing lanes.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When are you required to stop your vehicle?
options: a:Both when a police officer orders you to stop and when there is a red traffic light.,b:Only where there is a red traffic light.,c:Only at intersections where a police officer orders you to stop.
note: You must obey stop signals from officers and stop at steady or flashing red lights; follow directions of traffic officers at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you parallel park facing downhill, how should you turn your wheels?
options: a:Turn wheels sharply toward the curb or side of the road.,b:Turn wheels away from the curb.,c:Keep wheels straight.,d:Turn wheels toward the left only.
note: When parking downhill, turn your front wheels toward the curb or edge of the road so the vehicle will roll into the curb if it moves.

question: On the freeway behind a large truck, how should you follow compared to a passenger vehicle?
options: a:Farther behind the truck than you would when following a passenger vehicle.,b:Closely behind the truck in bad weather because the driver can see farther ahead.,c:No more than one car length behind the truck so the driver can see you.
note: Maintain a greater following distance behind trucks to compensate for their larger blind spots and longer stopping distances.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How should you change from one lane to another?
options: a:Gradually and carefully.,b:Quickly and often.,c:When a car is in your blind spot.
note: Change lanes smoothly and deliberately, signaling and checking mirrors and blind spots before doing so.

question: When a school bus ahead is stopped to load or unload children with flashing red lights and the stop arm extended, you must:
options: a:Come to a complete stop until all children have left the bus.,b:Come to a complete stop until the red lights stop flashing and the stop arm is withdrawn.,c:Change lanes and pass cautiously.,d:Slow down and proceed if no children are visible.
note: If a school bus is stopped with flashing red lights and stop arm extended, you must stop and remain stopped until the lights are off and the arm is withdrawn.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When leaving a driveway or alley to enter a sidewalk area, drivers should:
options: a:Stop only if pedestrians are present.,b:Stop before driving onto the sidewalk area.,c:Expect pedestrians to yield.,d:Proceed slowly without stopping.
note: Drivers must stop before driving onto a sidewalk or sidewalk area when entering the roadway from a private path to give pedestrians the right-of-way.

question: Continuous hard braking on ice and snow often:
options: a:Locks the front wheels of a vehicle, causing a loss of steering.,b:Helps you stop faster.,c:Keeps the brakes from freezing.
note: Hard braking on icy roads can lock wheels and cause a loss of steering control; brake gently and slowly.

question: If the roadway ahead is flooded, you should:
options: a:Slam on the brakes and drive through quickly.,b:Not drive through; turn around and find another route.,c:Drive in the center of the roadway only.,d:Drive slowly and test the depth with your tires.
note: Never attempt to drive through flooded roadways; even shallow water can hide hazards. Turn around and find another route.

question: If a child appears about to run into the street, you should:
options: a:Sound a sharp blast of your horn.,b:Start to prepare to slow down.,c:Flash your headlights.
note: Use a sharp horn blast to warn a child or pedestrian of imminent danger when they are about to enter the roadway.

question: When is it necessary to use low beam headlights?
options: a:On a well-lit street.,b:On a freeway.,c:In fog.,d:Only in rural areas.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or mist because high beams reflect and impair visibility.

question: At a railroad crossing you must:
options: a:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings and watch for multiple trains (both),b:Watch for vehicles that must stop at all railroad crossings (only),c:Watch for multiple trains (only).
note: Approach railroad crossings with caution and be aware of vehicles that are required to stop and the possibility of multiple trains.

question: What must you do when you approach an octagonal sign?
options: a:Stop.,b:Slow.,c:Turn.
note: An octagonal (eight-sided) sign always means STOP; come to a complete stop and yield to traffic or pedestrians before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A lane control sign showing an arrow with 'ONLY' above your lane means you should:
options: a:Travel in the direction of the arrow.,b:Always change lanes immediately.,c:Look for a destination sign to follow.,d:Ignore the sign if traffic is light.
note: Lane control signs require you to move in the direction indicated by the arrow for that lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When approaching a roundabout, you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Maintain your speed.,c:Increase your speed.
note: Roundabouts are designed to be negotiated at lower speeds; slow down as you approach.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing another vehicle you should:
options: a:Pass the vehicle as safely and as quickly as possible.,b:Drive at the same speed as the vehicle you are passing.,c:Pass the vehicle as slowly as possible.
note: Complete passing maneuvers promptly and return to your lane only when it is safe to do so.

question: If you must park where parking is not typical, what should you do?
options: a:Make sure your vehicle is visible to drivers approaching from any direction.,b:Park with your reverse lights on.,c:Park five feet from the curb.
note: When parking in an unusual area, ensure your vehicle is visible to oncoming traffic so it does not become a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How must you yield to an emergency vehicle using siren and lights?
options: a:Drive as close to the right edge as possible and stop.,b:Move into the right lane and drive slowly until it passes.,c:Stop immediately even if you are in an intersection.,d:Continue driving and ignore it if it is in another lane.
note: Yield to emergency vehicles by pulling to the right edge of the road and stopping; avoid stopping in an intersection.

question: Yellow centerlines separate which type of traffic?
options: a:Traffic moving in opposite directions on two-way roads.,b:Traffic lanes on one-way streets.,c:All carpool lanes from regular traffic lanes.
note: Yellow lines mark the center of two-way roads, separating opposing directions of traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When exiting an interstate, when should you begin to reduce your speed?
options: a:Immediately upon entering the deceleration lane.,b:About halfway through the deceleration lane.,c:As you approach the deceleration lane.
note: Maintain highway speed until you enter the deceleration lane, then slow to the advised exit speed.

question: Which statement about blind spots is true?
options: a:Blind spots are eliminated if you have one outside mirror.,b:Large trucks have larger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,c:You can check blind spots using only the rearview mirror.,d:Blind spots are not a concern with modern vehicles.
note: Even with mirrors, vehicles have blind spots; large trucks have much bigger blind spots than passenger vehicles.

question: In traffic moving at about 50–55 mph, you are least likely to have an accident if you:
options: a:Stay within that speed range.,b:Drive a few miles per hour faster than most other vehicles.,c:Drive a few miles per hour slower than most other vehicles.
note: Traveling consistently with the flow of traffic (within posted limits) reduces the likelihood of collisions caused by speed differentials.

question: If a tire suddenly blows out while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Grip the steering wheel firmly, slow down, and exit the traffic lane.,b:Brake hard and steer toward the right edge of the roadway.,c:Pump the brakes rapidly.
note: On a blowout, hold the wheel firmly, ease off the accelerator, slow gradually, and steer safely out of traffic before stopping.

question: What term refers to the amount of alcohol in a person's blood?
options: a:Blood alcohol concentration (BAC).,b:Implied consent (IC).,c:Rate of alcohol consumption (RAC).
note: Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) measures the percentage of alcohol in the bloodstream and indicates impairment level.

question: Which activity will slow your reaction time?
options: a:Drinking alcohol.,b:Sleeping.,c:Working hard.
note: Alcohol reduces reflexes, impairs judgment, and slows reaction time, negatively affecting driving skills.

question: If a traffic signal ahead is showing a steady yellow and you have not entered the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.,c:Speed up to beat the red light.
note: A steady yellow means the light is about to turn red; stop safely if you have not yet entered the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Collisions are more likely when:
options: a:All vehicles travel at the same speed.,b:One lane travels faster than other lanes.,c:One vehicle travels noticeably faster or slower than the flow of traffic.,d:Everyone maintains proper speed.
note: Collisions are more likely when a vehicle travels significantly faster or slower than surrounding traffic flow.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach an intersection with your view of cross traffic blocked, what should you do?
options: a:Stop, then inch forward until you can see clearly in both directions.,b:Slow down and look both ways.,c:Maintain your speed and look both ways.
note: If visibility is obstructed, stop and slowly creep forward until you can see cross traffic clearly before proceeding.

question: A pentagon-shaped sign is used to indicate:
options: a:A school zone or school crossing.,b:A stop sign.,c:A regulatory sign.
note: A five-sided sign typically warns drivers of school zones or school crossings where children may be present.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If traffic is merging into your lane on the freeway you should:
options: a:Make room for the merging traffic if possible.,b:Assert your right-of-way by driving faster.,c:Always maintain your position.
note: When safe, adjust speed or change lanes to allow merging vehicles to enter smoothly.

question: If pedestrians are illegally crossing in the middle of the street, what should you do?
options: a:Must stop for them.,b:Do not have to stop for them.,c:Should honk your horn at them.
note: You must yield to pedestrians at all times, even if they are crossing where they should not be.

question: What should you do to help avoid skidding on slippery surfaces?
options: a:Slow down before entering curves and intersections.,b:Shift to a lower gear after starting down a steep hill.,c:Speed up to enter curves and slow down to exit them.
note: Slow before curves and intersections; braking on a curve can cause loss of traction and lead to a skid.

question: If a tire suddenly goes flat while you are driving, you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and avoid heavy braking.,b:Rapidly pump the brake pedal several times.,c:Press down on the brake pedal as hard as you can.
note: Grip the wheel, ease off the accelerator, and slow gradually before pulling off the road safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it safe to return to your lane after passing another vehicle?
options: a:When you can see both headlights of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:When you have cleared the front bumper of the passed vehicle.,c:When you are 50 feet in front of the passed vehicle.
note: Return to your lane only after you can see the passed vehicle's headlights in your rearview mirror to ensure adequate space.

question: If your vehicle develops a mechanical problem while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Put on your hazard lights and pull off the road.,b:Stop in your lane and put on your hazard lights.,c:Signal and pull into the slow lane.
note: If possible, get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic, and turn on emergency flashers to warn other road users.

question: Driving under the influence of any medication that impairs you is:
options: a:Never permitted under any circumstances.,b:Allowed if you don't feel drowsy.,c:Allowed if prescribed by a physician.,d:Permitted if you read the medication label.
note: It is illegal to drive while impaired by any substance—prescription, over-the-counter, or illegal drugs—that affects your ability to drive safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To avoid traffic merging from right-side on-ramps while on an interstate, what is the best action?
options: a:Maintain your speed and position.,b:Change lanes to the left.,c:Slow down.
note: When traffic allows, move out of the right-hand lane to let vehicles merge from on-ramps on the right.

question: If you approach a stopped school bus with flashing lights and its arm extended, you must:
options: a:Stop and remain stopped until the arm is retracted and the bus moves.,b:Proceed at 15 mph if no children are present.,c:Proceed at normal speed while watching for children.
note: You must stop for a school bus with flashing lights and extended arm until it resumes motion or the arm is withdrawn.

question: What do double solid yellow lane markings mean?
options: a:No passing from either direction.,b:Passing allowed from both directions.,c:The right lane may pass.,d:Passing allowed only during daytime.
note: Double solid yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic and indicate passing is prohibited for both directions.

question: When driving behind another vehicle at night you should:
