options: a:Keep your headlights on the low beam setting.,b:Use your high beam headlights.,c:Use your high beam headlights until you are within 10 feet of the vehicle ahead.
note: Use low beams when following another vehicle so you don't blind the driver ahead.

question: Why should motor vehicle operators give extra space to children on bicycles?
options: a:Children lack adult reflexes.,b:They are smaller and harder to see.,c:Both lack of reflexes and smaller size make them unpredictable.,d:They always stop at intersections.
note: Children are less predictable and harder to see; give them extra space, especially near schools and playgrounds.

question: If you park facing uphill with a curb, set the parking brake and which way should you turn the front wheels?
options: a:Turn the front wheels away from the curb.,b:Leave the front wheels straight.,c:Turn the front wheels toward the curb.
note: When parking uphill with a curb, turn the wheels away from the curb so the vehicle will roll into the curb if brakes fail.

question: A broken yellow line beside a solid yellow line means:
options: a:Passing is permitted from the side next to the broken yellow line.,b:Passing is permitted from the side next to the solid yellow line.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.
note: When a broken line is next to a solid line, passing is allowed for the side with the broken line only.

question: If your wheels drop off the edge of the pavement, what should you do first?
options: a:Wait until it is safe to do so, then gradually re-enter the roadway.,b:Stop.,c:Turn back onto the roadway immediately.
note: Do not turn back onto the pavement immediately; slow down, check traffic, and re-enter the roadway gradually when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal turns from green to steady yellow as you approach, what should you do?
options: a:Speed up to clear the intersection before it turns red.,b:Come to a safe stop if you have not entered the intersection.,c:Proceed with caution through the intersection.,d:Stop immediately even if already in the intersection.
note: A steady yellow means the signal is about to turn red. If you have not entered the intersection, slow and stop safely; do not speed up to beat the red light.

question: Temporary construction and maintenance signs have what color scheme?
options: a:Orange background with black writing.,b:Red background with green writing.,c:Yellow background with blue writing.
note: Work zone signs are orange with black text or symbols to alert drivers to construction and maintenance hazards.

question: A flashing red traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:The same thing as a stop sign.,b:The same thing as a yield sign.,c:The light is about to turn green.
note: A flashing red light requires a full stop, yielding to traffic and pedestrians, then proceed when clear.

question: Which statement about railroad crossings is true?
options: a:You must stop at a railroad crossing when directed to do so by a flagger or stop sign.,b:You have the right-of-way at a railroad crossing and do not need to stop.,c:You should put on your cruise control near a railroad crossing.
note: Obey stop signs, flaggers, and warning signals at railroad crossings; stop when directed for safety.

question: What mindset should you have when driving in a construction zone?
options: a:Expect the unexpected.,b:Slightly increase your speed.,c:Expect construction workers to yield to motorists.
note: Construction zones often have unexpected conditions; slow down and drive cautiously for the safety of workers and drivers.

question: If you park facing uphill where there is no curb, set the parking brake and:
options: a:Turn your wheels toward the edge of the road.,b:Keep your wheels facing straight.,c:Turn your wheels away from the edge of the road.
note: Turning wheels toward the edge will cause the vehicle to roll away from traffic if the brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes, which action should you never take?
options: a:Cross the centerline in an intersection.,b:Check your blind spots by looking over your shoulder.,c:Check for other drivers moving into the same lane.
note: Never attempt to change lanes or pass in an intersection; always check mirrors and blind spots before moving laterally.

question: When a car with very bright headlights approaches at night you should:
options: a:Glance toward the right edge of your lane.,b:Stop until the other driver passes.,c:Look below their headlights.
note: Avoid looking directly at bright headlights; look to the right edge of your lane until the vehicle passes.

question: How dangerous is backing up a vehicle?
options: a:Always dangerous.,b:Dangerous if you have a helper.,c:Only dangerous in large vehicles.
note: Backing up is inherently risky because visibility is limited; take extra care whenever reversing.

question: To avoid becoming an aggressive driver you should:
options: a:Relax and concentrate on driving.,b:Drive above the posted speed limit.,c:Tailgate the driver in front of you.
note: Stay calm, drive within the speed limit, and avoid taking other drivers' actions personally.

question: How should you react when a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane is crossing the street?
options: a:You must always yield the right-of-way.,b:You must tell them where to cross the street.,c:You only have to yield if you are at a corner.
note: Drivers must always yield to pedestrians who are blind or partially blind, such as those using a guide dog or white cane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering an interstate highway from an entrance ramp, you should:
options: a:Check for cars, increase your speed to match the flow of traffic, and merge when it is clear.,b:Stop, check for cars, and enter when safe.,c:Check for cars and reduce your speed to 25 mph before entering the traffic lane.
note: Use the acceleration lane to get up to speed with highway traffic and merge smoothly when safe.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which lane should you be in before turning left from a one-way street?
options: a:The lane nearest the left curb.,b:The lane nearest the center of the street.,c:The lane nearest the right curb.
note: When turning, start from the lane closest to the direction you will travel; from a one-way street turning left, use the lane nearest the left curb.

question: Defensive driving can best be described as:
options: a:Using safe driving strategies to prevent crashes.,b:Driving aggressively.,c:More dangerous than not driving defensively.
note: Defensive driving means anticipating hazards, adjusting to conditions, and driving to prevent collisions.

question: When driving in work zones, you should:
options: a:Avoid tailgating and keep a safe following distance.,b:Pass the driver in front of you as soon as you can.,c:Follow the driver in front of you closely.
note: Work zones require increased following distances and care to protect workers and equipment.

question: In inclement weather you should:
options: a:Steer and brake smoothly.,b:Steer off the road.,c:Drive in a low gear.
note: Smooth steering and braking help maintain traction and control in poor weather conditions.

question: To avoid hydroplaning while driving in rainy conditions you should:
options: a:Slow down.,b:Drive at a speed appropriate for ideal conditions.,c:Apply your brakes as soon as your car starts to skid.
note: Slowing down reduces the chance that your tires will lose contact with the road surface.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: A prudent driver should:
options: a:Assume all other drivers obey right-of-way rules.,b:Assume most drivers obey the rules.,c:Always be prepared to yield right-of-way to avoid collisions.,d:Never yield as you have the right-of-way.
note: Even if you have the legal right-of-way, be prepared to yield if it prevents a collision; don't assume others will follow the rules.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you approach a green light but traffic is blocking the intersection, what should you do?
options: a:Partially enter to establish right-of-way.,b:Do not enter the intersection until you can clear it completely.,c:Enter and wait in the intersection until traffic clears.,d:Speed up to beat the congestion.
note: Even on a green light, do not enter an intersection unless you can get completely through without stopping and blocking it.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering a roadway from an alley or driveway, where must you stop?
options: a:At the sidewalk.,b:Honk your horn.,c:At a speed of 15 mph.
note: When entering a roadway from an alley, driveway, or building, stop before reaching the sidewalk to check for pedestrians and traffic.

question: A broken yellow centerline next to your lane means:
options: a:Passing is not permitted.,b:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow line on your side of the road indicates you may cross to pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: The best thing to do if you become tired while driving is to:
options: a:Stop to rest or change drivers.,b:Open a window.,c:Drink coffee.
note: If tired, stop at a safe place to rest or switch drivers; temporary measures like coffee are not reliable.

question: If a road is slippery, how should your following distance change?
options: a:Be farther from the car ahead than normal.,b:Be no different than normal.,c:Be closer to the car ahead than normal.
note: On slippery roads you need more stopping distance, so increase the distance between you and the vehicle ahead.

question: At a red light with a green arrow, when may you proceed in the arrow direction?
options: a:If you are in the proper lane and the intersection is clear.,b:Only after coming to a complete stop.,c:Only when the light changes to green.
note: A green arrow gives you the right to proceed in that direction if you are in the correct lane and the way is clear, but yield to pedestrians and other traffic already in the intersection.

question: If someone is tailgating you on a two-lane road and you cannot change lanes, what should you do?
options: a:Reduce your speed slowly to encourage the tailgater to drive around you.,b:Apply your brakes to slow down, then resume your original speed.,c:Speed up to increase the distance between you and the other car.
note: If you are being tailgated and cannot change lanes, slow down gradually to encourage the tailgater to pass; avoid sudden braking.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When turning left at an intersection you should:
options: a:Always yield to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.,b:Expect oncoming traffic to yield to you.,c:Turn quickly without checking for pedestrians.,d:Use the right lane when turning left.
note: Left-turning drivers must yield to oncoming traffic traveling straight and to pedestrians crossing the roadway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Under what condition may you drive in a High Occupancy Vehicle (HOV) lane?
options: a:If you drive faster than other traffic.,b:If your vehicle has multiple occupants.,c:If you are driving more slowly than traffic.,d:If it is late at night.
note: HOV lanes are reserved for vehicles with the required minimum number of occupants as shown by signage and diamond markings.

question: What does a double solid yellow centerline indicate about passing?
options: a:Not allowed from either direction.,b:Allowed only from your direction of travel.,c:Allowed from both directions.
note: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing for traffic in either direction.

question: When a bicyclist is making a left turn, what might they do?
options: a:They may use the left lane.,b:They may cut through all lanes.,c:They may wait on the side of the road.
note: Bicyclists are allowed to use the left lane to make a left turn; expect bicyclists to follow the same rules as motorists.

question: Which foot should you use for braking and accelerating?
options: a:Use your left foot to brake.,b:Use your right foot for both braking and accelerating.,c:Always brake abruptly to ensure stopping.,d:Alternate feet for comfort.
note: Use your right foot for both the accelerator and brake to avoid accidental simultaneous inputs and ensure smoother stops.

question: When driving at night, you should generally:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
note: Night driving reduces visibility and judgement; increase following distance and use appropriate beam settings for safety.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering and using a roundabout, drivers should:
options: a:Yield to traffic already circulating in the roundabout.,b:Yield to entering traffic.,c:Drive clockwise around the central island.,d:Stop before entering even if clear.
note: Roundabouts flow counterclockwise; drivers entering must yield to traffic already in the circle.

question: What is the legal status of holding a driver license?
options: a:Privilege, not a right.,b:Requirement.,c:Right, not a privilege.
note: A driver license is a privilege that must be earned and maintained, not an inherent right.

question: At a crosswalk you must:
options: a:Yield to pedestrians.,b:Pedestrians must yield to you.,c:Construction workers must yield to you.
note: Pedestrians have the right-of-way at crosswalks; vehicles must stop for them unless directed otherwise.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Excessive speed:
options: a:Increases the likelihood of serious bodily injury and death.,b:Saves time so you can get to your destination more quickly.,c:Helps you maneuver around obstacles.
note: Driving too fast increases crash severity and reduces reaction time; it does not reliably save time.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a traffic signal is green but a police officer signals you to stop, you should:
options: a:Obey the officer.,b:Obey the traffic signal.,c:Do what the vehicle in front of you does.
note: Follow directions from a police officer even if they contradict traffic signals or signs.

question: Excessive speed generally:
options: a:Does not increase crash risk.,b:Increases your ability to react to hazards.,c:Often leads to high-risk decision-making.,d:Is always safe on wide roads.
note: Excessive speed contributes to crashes and often causes riskier decisions and less time to react safely.

question: Which of these is a safe driving habit?
options: a:Using high beam headlights in fog.,b:Staring constantly at the road ahead.,c:Checking your rearview mirrors frequently.,d:Relying solely on side mirrors.
note: To stay aware of hazards, scan the road and check rearview mirrors every 2–5 seconds. Use low beams in fog, not high beams.

question: A stopped school bus is using its red flashing lights. What must you do?
options: a:Stop for as long as the red lights are flashing.,b:Slow to 25 mph and pass cautiously.,c:Stop and proceed when you think all children have exited the bus.
note: When a school bus displays flashing red lights, motorists must stop until the lights are turned off, unless the bus is on the opposite side of a divided highway.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When may you legally block an intersection?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If you entered the intersection on the green light.,c:During rush hour traffic.
note: You must not enter an intersection unless you can clear it; blocking an intersection can result in a citation.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Which of the following about driving speed is correct?
options: a:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality increases and you should increase your following distance.,b:As your speed increases, the chance of a fatality decreases.,c:Speed does not affect stopping distance.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distance and the severity of collisions, so following distance must increase with speed.

question: When driving on gravel or dirt roads, your tires have:
options: a:Less traction than on pavement, so you must slow down.,b:Better grip than on pavement.,c:Improved visibility compared to pavement.
note: Loose surfaces reduce traction and increase stopping distance and skid risk; slow down and drive cautiously.

question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic signal means you should:
options: a:Prepare to stop and yield the right-of-way to oncoming traffic.,b:Speed up so you can make the turn before the light changes.,c:You do not need to signal to turn from the indicated lane.
note: A steady yellow arrow warns that the protected turn is ending; yield to oncoming traffic and prepare to stop if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When another vehicle is passing you, you should:
options: a:Maintain a constant speed.,b:Brake hard.,c:Speed up.
note: Allow the passing vehicle to complete the maneuver safely by maintaining your speed or slowing slightly if needed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Drivers making a left turn must yield to which of the following?
options: a:Vehicles approaching from behind.,b:Oncoming traffic traveling straight or turning right.,c:No one; left-turning drivers always have the right-of-way.,d:Only to bicyclists.
note: Drivers turning left must yield to oncoming vehicles (including bicycles and motorcycles) that are going straight or turning right.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline between lanes indicate?
options: a:Both lanes go in the same direction.,b:Passing is permitted when it is safe.,c:Passing is prohibited.,d:Lane is reserved for carpool vehicles.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate opposite-direction lanes and indicate passing is allowed when there is no oncoming traffic.

question: From top to bottom, what is the correct order of traffic lights?
options: a:Red, yellow, green.,b:Red, green, yellow.,c:Green, yellow, red.,d:Yellow, red, green.
note: Standard vertical traffic signals are arranged red on top, yellow in the middle, and green on the bottom.

question: When driving in fog, you should:
options: a:Slow down and use your low beam headlights.,b:Slow down and use your high beam headlights.,c:Flash your lights to warn oncoming drivers.,d:Drive at normal speed if visibility seems okay.
note: In fog, slow down and use low beams; high beams reflect and reduce visibility. If you cannot see, pull off safely and wait.

question: If you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights behind you on a city street you should:
options: a:Drive to the right edge of the road and stop.,b:Stay in your lane, slow down, and let it pass.,c:Drive to the right edge of the road and slow down.
note: Pull to the right and stop to allow emergency vehicles to pass; if in an intersection, clear it first then stop.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Where is it safe to pass another vehicle?
options: a:Wherever signs and/or pavement markings permit passing.,b:Within an intersection where there are no oncoming vehicles.,c:Within a curve where there are no oncoming vehicles.
note: Only pass where signs and pavement markings allow; never pass in intersections, on curves, or where sight distance is limited.

question: A distraction while driving is:
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.,c:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.
note: A distraction is anything that diverts your attention from driving and can lead to collisions.

question: When following which vehicle should you leave extra space in front of you?
options: a:Motorcycle.,b:Passenger vehicle.,c:Station wagon.
note: Allow extra following distance for motorcycles because they can stop quickly and are harder to see at night.

question: When approaching a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, you should:
options: a:Stop until the person is well away from your path of travel.,b:Carefully drive around them.,c:Honk your horn as you proceed past them.
note: Yield and stop for blind pedestrians using a cane or guide dog until they are safely past your vehicle.

question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline indicate?
options: a:Do not pass.,b:Reduce your speed.,c:Traffic light ahead.
note: A solid yellow centerline on a two-lane road indicates a no-passing zone for traffic on the side with the solid line.

question: If you become drowsy while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Take a break.,b:Try to fight it.,c:Take some caffeine pills.
note: The safest response to drowsiness is to stop and rest, nap, or change drivers; caffeine or attempts to fight it are unreliable.

question: After stopping for a train at a railroad crossing, you should:
options: a:Look for a second train and wait for signal lights to stop flashing.,b:Wait only until the train has passed and then go immediately.,c:Proceed as soon as the train clears your lane.
note: Always check for additional trains on other tracks and wait for gates and signals to clear before proceeding.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: How do stopping distance and collision severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:They decrease as speed increases.,b:They remain unaffected by speed.,c:They increase as speed increases.,d:They vary unpredictably.
note: As speed increases, stopping distances and the force of collisions increase, raising risk of serious injury or death.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The vehicle on your left.,b:The driver who arrived before you.,c:The vehicle across from you.,d:The fastest vehicle.
note: At a stop sign on all corners, proceed in the order of arrival. If arriving simultaneously, yield to the vehicle on your left (yield right-of-way to the right).

question: If your vehicle starts to skid, what should you avoid doing?
options: a:Using the brakes.,b:Braking lightly.,c:Applying the brakes abruptly.
note: If your vehicle is skidding, avoid braking which can worsen the skid; steer to regain control and let speed reduce.

question: When should drivers yield the right-of-way to pedestrians in a crosswalk?
options: a:At all times.,b:Only if the pedestrians first wave to the driver.,c:Only if the pedestrians are not texting while walking.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in crosswalks under all conditions to prevent collisions.

question: When should you adjust your rearview and side mirrors?
options: a:Before you start driving.,b:Before you get into the car.,c:Whenever you need to use them.
note: Adjust mirrors after you are seated and before you move the vehicle; do not wait until you are driving to make mirror adjustments.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If two lanes move in your direction and you are in the left lane while others pass on the right, what should you do if the driver behind wishes to go faster?
options: a:Stay in your lane.,b:Drive onto the left shoulder to let them pass.,c:Move into the right lane when it is safe.,d:Stop suddenly to let them by.
note: If slower than surrounding traffic, move to the right lane when safe to allow faster vehicles to pass.

question: How do stopping distances and crash severity change as vehicle speed increases?
options: a:They increase as vehicle speed increases.,b:They are not affected by vehicle speed.,c:They decrease as vehicle speed increases.
note: Higher speeds increase stopping distances and the severity of collisions; driving faster raises crash risk and impact.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a police officer directs you through a red traffic light without stopping, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a complete stop before proceeding.,b:Go through the intersection without stopping.,c:Stop until the light turns green.
note: A police officer's traffic directions override traffic signals and signs; follow the officer's instructions.

question: Who may park in spaces reserved for handicap parking?
options: a:Anyone if all other spaces are full.,b:Drivers with the proper handicap plate or hanging tag.,c:People who are not feeling well.,d:Drivers transporting groceries.
note: You must have the appropriate license plate or hang tag showing the international symbol to park in a reserved handicap space.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To turn left from a multilane one-way street onto a one-way street you should start the turn from:
options: a:The lane closest to the left curb.,b:Any lane as long as it is safe.,c:The lane in the center of the road.
note: When turning left from a one-way street to another one-way street, begin from the far left lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When there are oncoming vehicles to your left and parked cars to your right, you should steer:
options: a:A middle course between the oncoming and parked vehicles.,b:Closer to the oncoming vehicles than the parked vehicles.,c:Closer to the parked vehicles than the oncoming vehicles.
note: Steering a middle course helps maximize clearance from both moving oncoming traffic and parked vehicles.

question: Which statement about driving and medications is true?
options: a:Prescription drugs are always safe if prescribed.,b:Most cold medications can cause drowsiness.,c:Over-the-counter drugs cannot impair driving at recommended doses.,d:Medications never affect driving ability.
note: Many over-the-counter cold medicines can make you drowsy and impair driving; all medications have potential effects on driving ability.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Before entering an intersection you should look:
options: a:Left, right, then left again.,b:Right only.,c:Left only.
note: Look left, then right, and left again before entering; vehicles from the left are closer and should be checked last.

question: Which headlights should you use when driving in fog?
options: a:Use your low beam headlights.,b:Use your parking lights.,c:Use your high beam headlights.
note: Use low beams in fog, rain, snow, or sleet; high beams reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: Why is it dangerous to follow a motorcycle too closely?
options: a:A motorcycle can stop much faster than a standard vehicle.,b:They brake more slowly than motor vehicles.,c:They do not follow the same rules as motor vehicles.
note: Motorcycles can stop quickly; following too closely reduces the time and space needed to avoid a collision with a motorcycle.

question: If a child is riding a bicycle near your vehicle, you should:
options: a:Beep your horn to warn them.,b:Expect the child to be fully in control.,c:Expect the unexpected and be prepared for sudden movements.,d:Speed up to pass quickly.
note: Children on bicycles are unpredictable; give them extra room and be prepared for sudden direction changes.

question: To reduce glare from oncoming headlights, what should you do?
options: a:Look briefly toward the right side of the road.,b:Stay focused on the centerline.,c:Flash your high beams.
note: Avoid staring at bright oncoming lights; glance briefly toward the right edge of the road, then return your view forward.

question: If you are driving next to a single broken white line, what is permitted?
options: a:You may cross the line to pass and change lanes.,b:You cannot cross the line to pass.,c:You may only cross the line to change lanes if you are in the left lane.
note: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving in the same direction and may be crossed for lane changes or passing when safe.

question: Roads are most slippery:
options: a:Just after it starts to rain.,b:When it has been raining hard for several hours.,c:When they are clean and dry.
note: Early in a rain event, oil and residue mix with water making the roadway especially slick.

question: When weather or light conditions require lights while driving, which should you use?
options: a:Parking lights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Low beam headlights.,d:Hazard flashers only.
note: Use low beam headlights in fog, rain, or snow; high beams will reflect and create glare, reducing visibility.

question: How many alcoholic drinks does it take to impair your driving ability?
options: a:One,b:Two,c:Three.
note: Even a single alcoholic drink can affect coordination, judgment, and reaction time; the safest choice is not to drive after drinking.

question: If you want to enter a freeway but cannot find a gap in traffic, you should:
options: a:Maintain your speed and force other drivers to make room.,b:Slow down on the ramp and wait for a gap.,c:Stop at the end of the ramp and wait.,d:Back up the ramp to look for a gap.
note: If you cannot safely merge, slow on the entrance ramp to wait for an adequate gap so you can accelerate to traffic speed.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a four-way stop where you reach the intersection at the same time as the driver on your left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:The driver on your right has the right-of-way.,b:You have the right-of-way.,c:The driver on your left has the right-of-way.
note: When vehicles arrive simultaneously at a multi-way stop, the vehicle on the right has the right-of-way.

question: What does a broken yellow centerline indicate?
options: a:Passing on the left is permitted when the way ahead is clear.,b:Passing is not permitted.,c:Passing on the right is permitted when the way ahead is clear.
note: A broken yellow centerline on your side means you may cross the centerline to pass if there is no oncoming traffic; do not cross a solid yellow to pass.

question: Which habit is part of defensive driving?
options: a:Keep your eyes moving to look for possible hazards.,b:Put one car length between you and the car ahead.,c:Look only at the car in front of you while driving.
note: Defensive drivers scan the road, check mirrors, and watch surrounding traffic rather than fixating straight ahead.

question: If you hit a parked vehicle and can't find the owner you must:
options: a:Leave a note with your name and address on the parked vehicle.,b:Call your insurance company when you get home.,c:Wait for the owner to return.
note: If you damage a parked vehicle, leave your contact information securely attached to the vehicle.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At a yield sign you must:
options: a:Always slow and proceed without stopping.,b:Yield right-of-way to cross traffic close enough to cause a conflict.,c:Yield only to vehicles coming from your right.,d:Stop completely regardless of traffic.
note: At a yield sign, slow or stop if necessary and give right-of-way to crossing or merging vehicles that are close enough to cause a conflict.

question: What does a curb painted red indicate?
options: a:The area is reserved for picking up or dropping off passengers.,b:No parking, standing, or stopping.,c:Loading zone.,d:Parking allowed for short stops only.
note: A red-painted curb means you may not stop, stand, or park in that area.

question: Before turning the ignition, what should you do regarding safety belts?
options: a:Both of the above.,b:Be sure all passengers have buckled their safety belts.,c:Buckle your safety belt.
note: Form a routine: before switching on the ignition, fasten your seat belt and make sure all passengers are belted.

question: What is distracted driving?
options: a:Anything that takes your attention away from driving.,b:Anything that causes evasive action while driving.,c:Anything that causes you to pay more attention to driving.
note: Distracted driving includes anything that takes your eyes, hands, or mind off driving and is a major cause of collisions.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you enter a roundabout, who must you yield to?
options: a:Both pedestrians and bicyclists and traffic already in the roundabout.,b:Any car already within the roundabout.,c:Any crossing pedestrians and bicyclists.
note: When entering a roundabout, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists and to any traffic already circulating in the roundabout.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you encounter a flashing red traffic light you must:
options: a:Treat the intersection as if it is controlled by a stop sign.,b:Are traveling in the wrong direction.,c:May not proceed until it changes to green.
note: A flashing red light is equivalent to a stop sign: stop, yield, and proceed when safe.

question: For drivers age 21 and older, what blood alcohol concentration (BAC) is illegal?
options: a:0.08 percent.,b:0.05 percent.,c:0.02 percent.
note: Drivers aged 21 or older are legally impaired at a BAC of 0.08% or higher; driving after any amount of alcohol is unsafe.

question: If you see pedestrians near the roadway, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down and pass with caution.,b:Sound your horn and maintain your speed.,c:Speed up to clear the area quickly.
note: Watch for pedestrians who may enter the roadway; slow down and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: If the broken yellow line is beside your lane when the center is marked with a solid and a broken yellow line, what does it mean?
options: a:You may pass other vehicles to the left when no oncoming traffic is present.,b:You are not allowed to pass in this area.,c:You are only allowed to make right turns in this area.
note: A broken yellow line beside your lane indicates you may pass when it is safe and no oncoming traffic is present; the solid line side may not pass.

question: Alcohol at any concentration acts as which of the following?
options: a:A stimulant.,b:A depressant.,c:An antihistamine.,d:Neither of the above.
note: Alcohol is a depressant and slows nerve impulses and bodily functions, impairing judgment, concentration, and alertness.

question: What is the only effective method to remove alcohol from the body?
options: a:Drink strong coffee.,b:Wait.,c:Take a cold shower.,d:Chew gum.
note: Time is the only way to remove alcohol from your system; other remedies do not reduce blood alcohol content.

question: What should you do about medicine before driving?
options: a:Consult your doctor or pharmacist about the effects before driving.,b:Have someone follow you home.,c:Keep your window open and drive more slowly.
note: Both prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving. Ask a medical professional about side effects before driving.

question: At a red traffic light displaying a green arrow for your lane, when may you proceed?
options: a:You are in the proper lane and the roadway is clear.,b:You first come to a complete stop.,c:You wait until the light changes to green.
note: A green arrow allows movement in the arrow's direction if you are in the corresponding lane and the way is clear.

question: What is the first ability affected by alcohol?
options: a:Vision.,b:Judgment.,c:Balance.,d:Hearing.
note: Judgment is typically the first mental ability reduced by alcohol, leading to poor decisions and impaired driving skills.

question: Which of the following affects how alcohol is absorbed by an individual?
options: a:Weight,b:Height,c:Intelligence,d:None of the above.
note: Factors affecting alcohol absorption include weight, biological sex, food in the stomach, and the amount consumed; weight is one of them.

question: You should allow an extra cushion of space when following:
options: a:A driver who cannot see the rear of their vehicle.,b:A small passenger car.,c:A station wagon.
note: Large vehicles or those towing trailers may have limited rear visibility; increase following distance to see around them.

question: When a school bus is picking up or dropping off children, drivers must:
options: a:Stop regardless of direction of travel.,b:Stop only when traveling in the same direction as the bus.,c:Slow down and be prepared to stop.,d:Pass cautiously at 10 mph.
note: You must stop for a school bus that is loading or unloading children, regardless of the direction you are traveling, unless on a divided highway where rules differ.

question: What type of information do blue traffic signs provide?
options: a:Motorist services (rest areas, hospitals),b:Construction and maintenance details.,c:Mileage and distance information.,d:Regulatory instructions.
note: Blue roadway signs are service signs that tell drivers about motorist services like rest areas, food, and hospitals.

question: If the rear of your vehicle is skidding left, what is the correct steering action?
options: a:Turn your steering wheel to the left to correct the skid.,b:Not turn your steering wheel.,c:Turn your steering wheel to the right to correct the skid.
note: In a skid, steer in the direction of the skid to help realign the vehicle; release the accelerator and avoid braking unless necessary.

question: When driving at night you should:
options: a:Increase your following distance.,b:Always use your high beams.,c:Look directly at the headlights of an oncoming vehicle.
note: Increase following distance at night and use headlights correctly; avoid looking directly at oncoming beams.

question: When driving in fog, which lighting choice is recommended?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:Four-way flashers.,c:High beam headlights.
note: Low beam headlights improve visibility in fog; high beams can worsen it by reflecting off the moisture.

question: What should you avoid doing when driving through a construction zone?
options: a:Stop to watch the workers.,b:Pass the zone carefully and do not slow to 'rubberneck'.,c:Decrease your following distance.
note: Drive carefully through work zones and do not slow down to look; maintain a safe following distance for everyone's safety.

question: If your vehicle begins to lose traction due to water on the road, you should:
options: a:Slow down gradually and not apply the brakes.,b:Drive at a constant speed to gain better traction.,c:Apply the brakes firmly to prevent your vehicle from sliding.
note: When hydroplaning, ease off the gas and let the vehicle slow; avoid braking until you regain traction.

question: What do broken yellow lines on the center of the pavement indicate?
options: a:Separate lanes of traffic moving in opposite directions and passing is permitted.,b:Indicate no passing zones.,c:Separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.
note: Dashed yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions and allow passing when it is safe to do so.

question: You can help keep the driver behind you a safe distance away by:
options: a:Maintaining a steady speed.,b:Driving 10 mph faster than the car behind you.,c:Driving 10 mph slower than the car behind you.
note: Keeping a steady speed and signaling early helps drivers behind maintain a safe following distance.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you enter a left-turn lane with oncoming traffic present, what should you do?
options: a:Signal before you arrive at the intersection.,b:Move to the left of the center lane.,c:Turn your front wheels to the left to be prepared to turn.
note: Signal about 100 feet before the turn and keep your wheels straight until you actually begin the turn to avoid being pushed into traffic if hit from behind.

question: When is it permissible to pass on the right shoulder of the road?
options: a:Never.,b:When the car ahead is turning left.,c:When the vehicle ahead is driving too slowly.,d:When traffic is stopped in your travel lane.
note: You may not drive off the pavement or onto the shoulder to pass. Passing on the right shoulder is not permitted.

question: Which of the following commonly contributes to traffic crashes?
options: a:Exceeding the posted speed limit or driving too fast for conditions.,b:Getting adequate rest and staying alert.,c:Scanning the environment and staying focused on driving.
note: Driving over the speed limit or too fast for conditions is a common factor in crashes; match speed to conditions and traffic flow.

question: A flashing yellow traffic signal indicates that you should:
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Come to a complete stop as quickly as possible.,c:Stop and proceed only when the intersection is clear.
note: A flashing yellow warns you to reduce speed and use caution; you do not need to stop unless conditions require it.

question: Regulatory traffic signs are typically what color background?
options: a:Yellow.,b:White.,c:Green.
note: Regulatory signs convey traffic laws and are commonly white rectangles or squares with black, red, or green text or symbols.

question: Work zone barriers, drums, cones, and signs are used to:
options: a:Keep traffic out of hazardous work zones.,b:Make drivers angry about slow traffic.,c:Inconvenience drivers.
note: These devices are placed to protect workers and drivers by guiding traffic away from hazards in work zones.

question: You may not park within how many feet of a railroad crossing?
options: a:50 feet,b:75 feet,c:100 feet.
note: Do not park within 50 feet of a railroad crossing so your vehicle does not block the crossing or create a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering the interstate on a short ramp with no acceleration lane, what is the correct procedure?
options: a:Speed up and enter the interstate only after you have identified a gap in traffic.,b:Immediately enter the far-right traffic lane and speed up to match traffic.,c:Use the shoulder of the main road to get up to the speed of traffic.
note: On a short ramp without an acceleration lane, wait for a safe gap, then accelerate and merge into traffic safely.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the proper way to make a right turn?
options: a:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the right curb before turning.,b:Signal, slow down, and get into the lane closest to the centerline before turning.,c:Approach the corner in the lane nearest the right curb, but move toward the middle before turning.
note: Signal, slow, and make the turn from the lane nearest the right curb or edge of the road, staying close to the curb.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You should use your horn when:
options: a:It may help prevent a collision.,b:Another vehicle is in your way.,c:Another driver makes a mistake.
note: Use the horn only when necessary to avoid collisions or to alert others to your presence.

question: To reduce the risk of hydroplaning in wet weather, you should:
options: a:Decrease your speed.,b:Put on your cruise control to maintain a constant speed.,c:Move to the shoulder as soon as it starts to rain.
note: Lower speed in wet conditions so tires can channel water and maintain traction with the road.

question: At dawn, dusk, and in rain or snow, a good way to let others know you are there is to turn:
options: a:On your headlights.,b:On your parking lights.,c:Up the instrument panel lights.
note: Use your headlights when visibility is reduced so other drivers can see your vehicle.

question: When following a motorcycle, you should:
options: a:Allow a larger following distance.,b:Be ready to use your horn.,c:Drive more slowly than posted speeds.
note: Give motorcycles extra following distance (3–4 seconds) so you can react to sudden stops or loss of control.

question: If the driver ahead stops at a crosswalk, what should you do?
options: a:Cautiously pass the vehicle at about 10 mph.,b:Stop and proceed only after all pedestrians have crossed.,c:Change lanes and go around the stopped vehicle.,d:Sound your horn and drive around them.
note: You must not pass a stopped vehicle at a crosswalk; there may be pedestrians crossing that you cannot see. Wait until all pedestrians are clear.

question: If your car begins to skid out of control, you should:
options: a:Stay off the brakes.,b:Apply the brakes lightly.,c:Pump the brakes.
note: During a skid, avoid braking and focus on steering to regain control until traction returns.

question: Which statement about blind spots is correct?
options: a:Large trucks have bigger blind spots than most passenger vehicles.,b:They are eliminated if you have one outside mirror on each side of the vehicle.,c:Blind spots can be checked by looking in your rearview mirrors.
note: Large trucks have substantial blind spots that drivers of smaller vehicles should avoid; mirrors do not eliminate all blind spots.

question: When traveling through a work zone, what should you generally do?
options: a:Maintain your normal speed the whole way through the zone.,b:Reduce your speed and be prepared to stop.,c:Increase your speed to get through the zone as quickly as possible.
note: Slow down, obey posted work zone speed limits, and be prepared for sudden stops or workers and equipment near the roadway.

question: An orange and red triangular sign on the back of a vehicle indicates:
options: a:Slow-moving vehicle.,b:The vehicle has the right-of-way.,c:Shoulder work ahead.
note: An orange and red triangle warns that the vehicle travels at low speeds and drivers should use caution.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should:
options: a:Rely only on the rearview mirror.,b:Look over your shoulder in the direction you plan to move.,c:Rely only on the left side mirror.,d:Signal and immediately change without checking.
note: Glance over your shoulder in the direction of the lane change to check blind spots before moving over.

question: In a vehicle with airbags, where is it safest for children age 12 and under to ride?
options: a:The bed of a pick-up truck.,b:The back seat.,c:The front seat.
note: Airbags are designed for adult protection and can be dangerous to small children; kids age 12 and under should ride in the back seat.

question: A steady green traffic light at an intersection means:
options: a:You may continue through the intersection at a safe and reasonable speed, if it is clear to do so.,b:Increase your speed.,c:Adjust your mirrors.
note: A steady green light allows you to proceed, but you must yield to traffic or pedestrians already in the intersection.

question: What can you do to help reduce incidents of road rage?
options: a:Always signal your intention when changing lanes.,b:Use your horn frequently.,c:Talk on your cell phone while driving.
note: Signal your intentions, obey traffic laws, and drive courteously to reduce the likelihood of road rage incidents.

question: When stopping on snow or ice in a vehicle equipped with ABS, you should:
options: a:Press and hold the brake pedal firmly.,b:Pump the brakes.,c:Stay off the brakes and wait for the car to drift to a stop.
note: With ABS, press and hold the brake firmly; the system will modulate braking for you to help maintain steering control.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an intersection with a yield sign, what must you do?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to traffic close enough to cause a conflict.,b:Slow down but never stop.,c:Must yield to vehicles only on your right.
note: At a yield sign you must give way to traffic already in the lane you plan to enter and be prepared to stop if necessary.

question: A pedestrian started crossing after the Don't Walk signal began flashing and is in the roadway when your light turns green. What should you do?
options: a:Wait until the pedestrian crosses the street before proceeding.,b:Proceed if the pedestrian is not in your lane.,c:Proceed if you have the right-of-way.
note: You must yield to pedestrians already in the roadway; wait until they have finished crossing before proceeding.

question: If you see a pedestrian using a guide dog or carrying a white cane, you should:
options: a:Expect the pedestrian to yield to you.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the pedestrian.,c:Honk to alert them of your presence.,d:Drive slowly behind them until they move.
note: Blind or partially blind pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane must be yielded to; give them the right-of-way.

question: What is the primary purpose of rumble strips on the roadway?
options: a:Through vibration and sound, they alert inattentive drivers that their vehicle has left the travel lane.,b:They test a vehicle's shock absorbers.,c:They alert drivers to potential tire problems.
note: Rumble strips produce noise and vibration to warn drowsy or inattentive drivers that they are leaving the travel lane or approaching a hazard.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: You park uphill on a two-way road with no curb. Which way should you turn your front wheels?
options: a:Turn the wheels to the right, toward the side of the road.,b:Turn the wheels to the left, toward the center of the road.,c:Point wheels straight ahead.
note: On an uphill slope with no curb, turn wheels toward the roadside so the vehicle will roll away from the center of the road if brakes fail.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: At an uncontrolled intersection where you arrive at the same time as vehicles on your right and left, who has the right-of-way?
options: a:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your right.,b:Yield the right-of-way to the vehicle on your left.,c:Wait until there are no vehicles at the intersection before proceeding.
note: When vehicles arrive at an uncontrolled intersection simultaneously, the driver on the right has the right-of-way.

question: Why should you use headlights on rainy, snowy, or foggy days?
options: a:To keep your engine warm.,b:So other road users can see your vehicle.,c:To warn others of bad weather conditions.,d:To improve fuel efficiency.
note: In poor weather visibility, headlights make your vehicle easier for others to see; if wipers are on you must also use low beam headlights.

question: If your tires seem to lose contact with the road (hydroplaning), what should you do?
options: a:Ease your foot off the gas pedal and stay off the brakes.,b:Slow down by pumping the brakes quickly and firmly.,c:Slow down by shifting into a lower gear.
note: When hydroplaning, gradually slow by easing off the accelerator and avoid braking or sharp steering until traction returns.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: It is unlawful to:
options: a:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone or over certain crossings (both violations),b:Pass another vehicle over a railroad crossing only.,c:Pass another vehicle in any marked no passing zone only.
note: You may not pass in marked no-passing zones, at railroad crossings, or where signs prohibit passing.

question: If you encounter a dust storm while driving, what should you do?
options: a:Slow down, pull completely off the road, turn off your lights, take your foot off the brake, and wait.,b:Be cautious and drive through it, since dust storms usually don't last long.,c:Slow down, pull completely off the road, turn on your lights, and wait.
note: In severe dust storms, get entirely off the roadway away from traffic, turn off lights and brakes, stay buckled in your vehicle, and wait for the storm to pass.

question: If you are crossing an intersection when an emergency vehicle with siren and lights approaches, what should you do?
options: a:Continue through the intersection, pull to the right, and stop.,b:Stop immediately in the intersection until it passes.,c:Pull to the right of the intersection and stop.
note: If already in the intersection, clear it, then pull to the right and stop to yield to emergency vehicles using lights or sirens.

question: If you approach an intersection showing a steady yellow light and have not entered it, what should you do?
options: a:Come to a safe stop.,b:Speed up to beat the red light.,c:Reduce your speed and proceed carefully through the intersection.
note: A steady yellow warns that the signal will soon be red; prepare to stop if you have not already entered the intersection.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: In which situation should your wheels NOT be pointed straight ahead?
options: a:When parked on a hill or sloping driveway.,b:When waiting to make a left turn at a traffic light.,c:When parked on the side of a level roadway where there is no curb.
note: When parked facing uphill or downhill, turn your wheels so the vehicle cannot roll into traffic if the brakes fail.

question: Which statement about bicyclists is correct?
options: a:Must follow the same laws as motorists.,b:Must stay in the right lane.,c:Should ride facing traffic.
note: Bicyclists are required to obey the same traffic laws as motor vehicle drivers and have the same rights and responsibilities on the road.

question: When merging onto an interstate, you should:
options: a:Select a safe gap and merge into traffic.,b:Merge across two lanes at once.,c:Always stop at the end of the ramp.,d:Enter at any speed and slow down once merged.
note: Find a sufficiently large gap in traffic and merge smoothly into the flow at an appropriate speed.

question: Large trucks are likely to lose speed when:
options: a:Driving up long or steep hills.,b:Driving down long, gradual hills.,c:Driving in long, gradual curves.
note: Trucks take longer to accelerate and may slow considerably when climbing long or steep grades.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you plan to pass another vehicle, you should:
options: a:Not assume the other driver will make space for you to return to your lane.,b:Assume the other driver will let you pass if you use your turn signal.,c:Assume the other driver will maintain a constant speed.
note: Never assume other drivers will yield; verify it is safe before you pass and return to your lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you face a green light but the intersection ahead is blocked by traffic, what should you do?
options: a:Stay out of the intersection until traffic clears.,b:Follow the other vehicles and enter the intersection.,c:Turn left and find another route.
note: Do not enter an intersection unless you can fully clear it; blocking an intersection can be illegal and dangerous.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: The posted maximum speed limit should be driven only under what conditions?
options: a:Under ideal conditions.,b:During the day.,c:During the night.
note: The posted maximum is the highest legal speed under ideal conditions; adjust speed for traffic, weather, and road conditions.

question: Which statement best describes how a defensive driver thinks?
options: a:They assume other drivers will always do the right thing.,b:They anticipate other drivers' possible actions and prepare to react.,c:They expect no breaks and give none.,d:They rely only on traffic signals.
note: Defensive drivers anticipate potential mistakes by others and are prepared to respond to avoid collisions.

question: Any amount of alcohol in the bloodstream may affect a driver's:
options: a:Right-of-way privileges.,b:Judgment and physical coordination.,c:Knowledge of traffic laws.,d:License class.
note: Even small amounts of alcohol can impair judgment and coordination and affect driving ability.

question: When driving at night on a dimly lit street, you should:
options: a:Drive slowly enough that you can stop within the area illuminated by your headlights.,b:Turn on your high beam headlights to better see the vehicles ahead of you.,c:Keep the instrument panel lights bright to be more visible to other drivers.
note: At night, slow down so you can stop within the distance illuminated by your headlights and use appropriate beam settings.

question: Traffic control devices in construction and maintenance work areas are what color?
options: a:Orange.,b:Red.,c:Yellow.
note: Orange signs, cones, and barriers are used to indicate construction and maintenance areas.

question: How can you best know where traffic is behind you?
options: a:Frequently check your rearview mirror.,b:Turn and look out your back window constantly.,c:Keep vehicles out of your blind spots only.,d:Use only side mirrors.
note: Regularly checking your rearview mirror helps you stay aware of traffic behind you and anticipate changes.

question: Extra space in front of a large truck is needed for:
options: a:The truck driver to stop the vehicle.,b:Other drivers to merge onto the freeway.,c:Other drivers when they want to slow down.
note: Large trucks need longer stopping distances than passenger cars; leave extra space in front of them.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When changing lanes you should never:
options: a:Change lanes abruptly or spontaneously.,b:Look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.,c:Check for other vehicles moving into the same lane.
note: Avoid sudden lane changes; always signal and check mirrors and blind spots first.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If a truck or bus is making a right turn where you also need to turn right, what should you do?
options: a:Wait until the truck or bus completes the turn before you turn.,b:Quickly turn before the truck or bus can.,c:Squeeze between the truck or bus and the curb.
note: Large vehicles may swing wide when turning; wait for them to finish their turn before making yours to avoid collision.

question: When is pavement most slippery during rainy conditions?
options: a:During the first half hour of rain.,b:One half hour after it stops raining.,c:If it has been raining all day.
note: Roads are especially slick during the first half hour of rain as oil and dirt mix with the water to form a greasy film.

question: If your car becomes disabled on the highway, you should:
options: a:Stop in the right travel lane.,b:Park with all four wheels off the traveled portion of the highway if possible.,c:Stop where you are and leave the vehicle.,d:Turn on high beams to signal for help.
note: If your vehicle is disabled, move it completely off the main-traveled portion of the road if you can, to avoid blocking traffic and reduce danger.

question: If you want to pass a pedestrian and an oncoming vehicle is approaching, you should:
options: a:Slow down and let the oncoming vehicle pass before you pass the pedestrian.,b:Keep driving at a steady speed; the oncoming vehicle must stop.,c:Honk to get the pedestrian to move over.
note: Handle one hazard at a time: let the oncoming vehicle pass, then pass the pedestrian only if safe to do so.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: As you approach the top of a hill, how should you prepare?
options: a:Prepare to stop, if needed.,b:Speed up slightly.,c:Maintain a steady speed.
note: Because you cannot see what is over the crest, reduce speed and be ready to stop if necessary.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If you continually pass other vehicles on a two-lane road by driving faster than others, you will:
options: a:Increase your chances of a collision.,b:Get you to your destination much more quickly and safely.,c:Help prevent traffic congestion.
note: Frequent passing on two-lane roads raises collision risk due to limited sight lines and opposing traffic.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When is it legal to make a left turn on a red light after stopping?
options: a:When you are on a one-way street turning onto another one-way street.,b:When you are traveling on a two-way street and turning onto a two-way street.,c:Whenever you yield to all other traffic at the intersection.
note: After a complete stop, you may turn left on red only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless signs prohibit it.

question: Within how many days must you notify the MVD of an address change?
options: a:10 days.,b:30 days.,c:45 days.,d:60 days.
note: You must notify the Arizona MVD of any change of name or address within 10 days of the change.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: To pass on a two-lane road you should:
options: a:Judge the distance to any oncoming vehicles.,b:Sound your horn as you pass.,c:Flash your headlights as you pass.
note: Ensure there is enough clear distance and time to pass safely before you move into the opposing lane.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When entering traffic after parking at a curb, you should:
options: a:Wait for a large enough gap to get up to the speed of traffic.,b:Drive more slowly than other traffic for 200 feet.,c:Enter after the first two vehicles pass.
note: When merging from a curb, wait for a gap that allows you to accelerate to the speed of traffic safely.

question: How far ahead should a driver typically look in city driving to avoid sudden stops or turns?
options: a:One city block.,b:Five feet.,c:Three city blocks.
note: In city driving, scanning at least one block ahead helps you anticipate hazards and avoid sudden maneuvers.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: Is it permissible to drive on the shoulder to pass a car?
options: a:Under no circumstances.,b:If the vehicle ahead of you is turning left.,c:If the shoulder is wide enough.
note: Never pass another vehicle by driving on the shoulder; it is unsafe and usually illegal.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: If another driver is passing you in a no passing zone, how should you respond?
options: a:Slow down and let the other driver safely return to the drive lane.,b:Pull off the road.,c:Maintain your speed and position.
note: Allow an unsafe passing vehicle to return to the travel lane by slowing and making it easier for them to re-enter.

question: If you see animals standing near the roadway, how should you proceed?
options: a:Slow down and proceed with caution.,b:Quickly swerve into the next lane.,c:Speed up to scare them away.
note: Animals near the road may bolt unpredictably; reduce speed and pass cautiously to avoid collisions.

question: A broken yellow line down the center of the road indicates:
options: a:Passing is permitted from either direction.,b:A construction zone is ahead.,c:Passing is not permitted from either direction.,d:Both lanes travel in the same direction.
note: Broken yellow lines between two-way traffic mean drivers may pass when it is safe and there is no oncoming traffic.

question: If a vehicle is equipped with airbags, what should you still do?
options: a:Seat belts should still be worn.,b:Seat belts do not need to be worn.,c:Seat belts should be worn behind the back.
note: Airbags supplement lap and shoulder belts; for best protection always wear the vehicle's seat belts in combination with airbags.

question: If you see orange construction signs and cones on a freeway, what should you expect?
options: a:Be prepared for workers and equipment ahead.,b:Change lanes and maintain your current speed.,c:Slow down because the lane ends ahead.
note: Work zone signs and cones warn of workers, equipment, and lane changes; reduce speed and be prepared to slow or stop.

question: Which driving skills are impaired by alcohol and/or drugs?
options: a:Reaction time and coordination.,b:Alertness and concentration.,c:All of the above.
note: Alcohol and many drugs depress the nervous system and reduce alertness, concentration, reaction time, and coordination.

question: Which practice blocks the smooth flow of traffic?
options: a:Slowing down to look at a collision scene.,b:Avoiding unnecessary lane changes.,c:Using public transportation instead of your vehicle.
note: Rubbernecking—slowing or stopping to look at a crash—creates congestion and contributes to further incidents.

question: [Removed - image-based question]
options: a:Right turns only.,b:Right turns permitted.,c:No passing zone.
note: Pennant-shaped yellow signs indicate a no passing zone.

question: If involved in a minor intersection collision with no injuries and little damage, you should:
options: a:Leave your vehicle in the traffic lane until police arrive.,b:Move your vehicle out of the traffic lane if possible.,c:Never move your vehicle under any circumstances.,d:Drive away if damage is minor.
note: If no one is injured and it is safe, move vehicles out of the traffic lane to reduce further hazards and wait for law enforcement if needed.

question: Which lights should you use in fog, rain, or snow to avoid reducing visibility?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Four-way flashers.
note: Use low beams in adverse weather; high beams can reflect and reduce your ability to see.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: When passing on the left, it is safe to move back into the right lane when:
options: a:You can see the front of the passed vehicle in your rearview mirror.,b:After about three seconds.,c:When you can no longer see the vehicle over your right shoulder.
note: Return to the driving lane only when you can clearly see the passed vehicle's front in your rearview mirror.

question: How much space should you normally leave between your vehicle and the one ahead?
options: a:Three to six seconds,b:One second,c:10 seconds
note: Under normal driving conditions maintain a three- to six-second following distance; increase that distance in poor weather or heavy traffic.

question: Which statement about drugs and driving is correct?
options: a:Only illegal drugs can impair driving.,b:Even over-the-counter drugs can impair driving.,c:Prescriptions are always safe if you feel fine.,d:Drugs have no effect when combined with alcohol.
note: Legal prescription and over-the-counter drugs can impair driving; it is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

question: Which lights improve visibility in rain or fog?
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Parking lights.
note: Low beams are best in rain, fog, snow, or sleet; high beams will reflect back and reduce visibility.

question: How are bicycles treated on roadways?
options: a:As hazards.,b:As vehicles.,c:As pedestrians.,d:As toys.
note: Bicycles are considered vehicles on roadways; bicyclists and motorists must follow the same traffic rules.

question: If there is no crosswalk and a pedestrian is crossing your lane, what must you do?
options: a:Stop and let the pedestrian finish crossing.,b:Make sure the pedestrian can see you before proceeding.,c:Cautiously drive around the pedestrian.
note: Drivers must yield to pedestrians in the roadway even if there is no marked crosswalk.

question: When driving in fog, rain, or snow, use:
options: a:Low beam headlights.,b:High beam headlights.,c:Fog lights only.
note: Low beams reduce glare and help you see better in fog, rain, or snow.

question: Must you yield to a pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog?
options: a:Only when the guide dog is leading the person across the street.,b:At all times.,c:Only if a crossing guard is present.
note: Pedestrians using a guide dog or white cane (with or without a red tip) must be given the right-of-way at all times.

section-name: Traffic Laws & Rules of the Road
question: What is the speed limit when approaching a school crossing if no other limit is posted?
options: a:15 mph.,b:10 mph.,c:25 mph.
note: Unless otherwise posted, the speed limit when approaching a school crosswalk is 15 mph to protect children crossing the road.

question: When exiting the freeway on a ramp that curves downhill, you should:
options: a:Slow to a safe speed before the curve.,b:Wait until you have entered the curve to begin braking.,c:Slow to the posted speed limit for the freeway.
note: Reduce speed before entering the curve; braking within a curve can cause loss of control.
